articles.title: 360 Fried Eggs
articles.body:
Serves: 1 people
Prep Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 4 minutes
Calories:143 calories


Ingredients:

  • 2 large eggs
  • Non-stick cooking spray
  • Salt and freshly ground pepper


Instructions:

  1. Crack the eggs into a small bowl.
  2. Heat the 11.5” Fry Pan over medium heat for 3 minutes.
  3. Lightly spray the pan with cooking spray 
  4. Gently crack the egg and empty into the pan. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
  5. Cook until the whites are set and the yolks are cooked through as desired.
  6. Gently flip the eggs using a spatula and continue cooking until the eggs have reached your desired level of doneness.
articles.author: Brittany Pitschman

articles.title: Classic Beef Stew
articles.body:
The unique design of our cookware encourages foods to release their own flavorful liquids, which is why our recipes call for so much less (if any at all) than other recipes. Rest assured — you’re about an hour away from a stew of tender of beef, bathed in plenty of rich, silky sauce.

Serves: 4 people
Prep Time: 20 minutes
Cooking Time: 3 hours
Calories:  521 calories

Ingredients:

  • 2 ½ pounds stew beef, preferably chuck 
  • 1 large onion, chopped large 
  • Salt
  •  1 1/2 cups low sodium chicken broth, beef broth, or water
  •  2 garlic cloves, minced
  •  1 teaspoon fresh chopped thyme or ½ teaspoon dried
  •  3 tablespoons all purpose flour
  •  2 tablespoons tomato paste
  •  1 cup dry red wine
  •  1 bay leaf
  •  Freshly ground black pepper
  •  6 small new potatoes, quartered
  •  2 carrots, chopped medium 
  • 1 ½ cups fresh or frozen peas

Instructions:

  1. Heat the 4-quart stock pot over medium heat for about 5 minutes until it’s hot enough that water droplets bead across the surface, about 5 minutes.
  2. Working in two batches, brown the beef on all sides in the hot, dry pan. (The meat will stick initially. It is ready to turn once it comes away from the pan with no resistance.) Transfer to a bowl and set aside.
  3. Add the onions, and ½ cup of the broth to the pot and stir up the browned bits. Cover and cook about 5 min until the onions are softened.
  4. Stir inthe garlic, and thyme cook uncovered for about 2 minutes.
  5. Stir in the flour and tomato paste and cook for about 5 minutes, stirring often.
  6. Stir in the wine, and remaining broth, scraping the bottom of the pot.
  7. Add the beef, and bay leaf, and season with salt and pepper.
  8. Cover and cook until steam just begins to escape from under the lid, about 10 minutes.
  9. Spin the lid to engage the vapor seal then immediately reduce the heat to low. Cook for 1 hour.
  10. Stir in the potatoes and carrots. Cover and cook for 45 to 60 minutes, or until the beef is very tender.
  11. Stir in the peas and cook for about 10 minutes until the peas are just tender. Serve.
articles.author: Brittany Pitschman

articles.title: Eggs Baked in Tomato Sauce
articles.body:
Perfect for brunch, lunch, or dinner. Serve with a green salad and slices of toasted, garlic-rubbed bread.

Serves: 4 people
Prep Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 6 minutes
Calories: 107 calories

Ingredients:

  • 1 1/4 cups 360 Marinara Sauce, or your favorite prepared sauce, chilled
  • 6 eggs
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper
  • 2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley


Instructions:

  1. Spread the tomato sauce in the 3.5 Quart Sauté Pan. Use a soupspoon to make six wells in the sauce.
  2. Crack an egg into a small, shallow cup or ramekin. Hold the cup as close to the sauce as possible and gently pour it into one of wells in the sauce. Repeat with the remaining eggs. Season the eggs with salt and pepper and sprinkle with the parsley.
  3. Cover the pan and cook over medium heat for about 5 minutes until steam just begins to escape from under the lid.
  4. Spin the lid to engage the vapor seal then immediately reduce the heat to low. Cook for 30 seconds.
  5. Remove from the pan from the heat and let stand, covered, for about 3 minutes until the whites are firm and the yolks are set, but still soft. (If the eggs are undercooked, replace the lid and let stand for another minute or two.) 
  6. To serve use a large spoon or spatula to transfer the eggs and sauce to plates.
articles.author: Brittany Pitschman

articles.title: Mediterranean Spice Burgers
articles.body:
Goes great with our 360 Pick-Up Sticks French Fries!

Serves: 4 people
Prep Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 15 minutes
Calories: 490 calories

Ingredients:

  • 1 lb. ground lamb
  • ½ lb. ground turkey
  • 1 teaspoon Mediterranean Spice Mix (Recipe below)
  • ¼ cup crumbled feta cheese (optional)

Mediterranean Spice Mix:
  • 2 teaspoons cumin seed
  • 1-teaspoon coriander seed
  • 1-teaspoon cardamom seed (Pods removed)
  • 1 stick of cinnamon (Broken into 2 pieces)
  • ¼ teaspoon cloves

Instructions:
  1. Mix together in a medium bowl the lamb, turkey, 1-teaspoon of the spice mix, and
  2. the feta cheese (if desired).
  3. Divide the mixture into four equal parts and form into burger patties.
  4. Sprinkle both sides of the patties with the Mediterranean Spice Mix.
  5. Heat the 360 by Americraft 3.5 quart sauté pan over medium heat. The pan is ready when sprinkled water droplets dance on the surface of the pan.
  6. Place the burger patties in the pan. (You should hear a definite sizzle.) Add 1teaspoon of water to the center of the pan. Cover the pan with the lid. Immediately reduce the heat to low.
  7. Cook the burgers for 4-5 minutes.
  8. Remove the lid. Turn the burgers. Replace the lid and cook on low until the burgers reach an internal temperature of 160 F. (Approximately 3-4 minutes)
  9. Transfer the burgers to a plate and allow them to rest for 5 minutes.
  10. Serve on a buttered, toasted hamburger roll with leaf lettuce, sliced tomato, shaved red onion and a big dollop of our *Yogurt-Cucumber Sauce.
*Tip: Make the patties thin with a well in the center. This will keep them in a nice burger shape during the cooking process.

Mediterranean Spice Mix:
  1. Toast the cumin, coriander, cardamom, cinnamon, and cloves in a dry 360 by Americraft 7” fry pan over medium heat for 3-4 minutes. Swirl the pan often to avoid burning the mix.
  2. Place the toasted spices in a spice mill and grind to a powder. Transfer the spices to a small jar or bowl.
  3. Add 2-Tablespoons of kosher salt and ¼-teaspoon of freshly ground black pepper to the mix.
  4. Stir to mix. In an airtight container, this spice mix should remain fresh for 6 months.

articles.title: Stovetop Gingerbread Cake

image.altText: Close-up of stovetop gingerbread cake showcasing candied ginger slices and a light glaze on a white plate

articles.body:
A quick and simple, but delicious cake; perfect for unexpected visitors.


Serves: 8 people
Prep Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Calories: 249 calories

Ingredients:

  • 1/3 c. Butter
  • 1/2 c. Boiling water
  • 1/4 c. Sugar
  • 1/2 c. Molasses
  • 1 Egg, beaten
  • 1 1/2 c. Flour
  • 1 tsp. Baking soda
  • 2 tsp. Ginger powder
  • 1 tsp. Ground cloves
  • 1/8 tsp. Salt
  • Parchment paper
  • Cooking Spray


Instructions:

  1. Combine butter and water in a heat safe, 2 cup, measuring cup; stir until the butter is melted. Add sugar, molasses and stir to combine. Add the beaten egg and stir to combine.
  2. Sift the flour, baking soda, ginger cloves and salt together into a bowl. Pour the liquid mixture into the flour mixture and stir until just combined.
  3. Cut a circle from the parchment paper the size of the bottom of the 2.3 Quart Casserole. Preheat the casserole over medium-low heat for 2-3 minutes. Spray the casserole with cooking spray and place the parchment paper circle inside the bottom of the pan.
  4. Pour the cake mixture into the prepared pan; place the pan back on medium-low heat and bake for 20-25 minutes. The cake is done when a toothpick is inserted in the center and comes out clean. 
  5. Remove the cake from the heat when the cake is done. Remove the lid and let the cake stand for 5 minutes to cool. After cooling, place a plate upside down over the casserole. Holding the plate and casserole together, flip the cake over. Remove the casserole and the parchment paper. Use a second plate and repeat the flip to turn the cake right side up. Let the cake cool for another 5 minutes.
  6. Serve with freshly whipped cream.
articles.author: Brittany Pitschman

articles.title: Pick-Up-Sticks Potato Fries

image.altText: Close-up of pick-up-sticks style potato fries showcasing thin julienned golden-brown sticks on a white plate

articles.body:
Do you remember the old children’s game? (If not, ask your mother!) These tasty fries are thinly julienned and fry up beautifully. Pair them with our Mediterranean Spice Burgers or Grateful Turkey Burgers. They are sure to add a “kick” to any football party or family dinner.


Serves: 4 people
Prep Time: 10 minutes
Cooking Time: 5 minutes
Calories: 69 calories

Ingredients:

  • 1 lb. Idaho baking potatoes, room temperature, skin on (Use the large bakers for better results.)
  • 6 cups peanut oil
  • Potato Spice Seasoning (recipe follows)


Instructions:

  1. Heat uncovered to 375 degrees F- 6 cups of peanut oil in the 360 by Americraft 4-quart stockpot.
  2. Julienne slice the potatoes lengthwise into strips that are 1/8” x 1/8”. Dry potatoes with paper toweling. 
  3. Fry potato sticks in small batches (1-cup) for one minute. (There should be no color to the potatoes-yet.) Using a spider mesh or a slotted spoon remove the potatoes from the oil and transfer them to a platter or bowl. *Be sure to bring the oil’s heat back up to 375 degrees F between batches. Repeat this process until all the potatoes have been par-fried.
  4. Fry the potatoes a second time (2 batches) for 1-2 minutes. The potato sticks should be deep golden brown. Remove them from the oil and transfer them to a paper lined platter or baking sheet.
  5. Sprinkle immediately with the *Potato Spice Seasoning.
  6. Potato Spice Seasoning Recipe: Combine in a small bowl: 1 Tablespoon kosher salt, 1-teaspoon smoked paprika, ½- teaspoon garlic powder, ¼-teaspoon onion powder, ¼-teaspoon freshly ground black pepper. (Remaining spice can be stored in an airtight container for up to 12 months.)


360 Tips: Keep your Pick-up Sticks Potato Fries warm between batches on a paper lined baking sheet in an oven set at 225 degrees F. Oil should never reach higher than 2/3 of the way up the sides of the pot during frying. *Caution - NEVER leave hot oil unattended. Hot oil can cause severe burns.
articles.author: Brittany Pitschman

articles.title: Get Well Soon
articles.body:
This is the soup everyone longs for but no one has the time to make. Our speedy version packs so much simmered-all-day flavor and comfort into one little hour that you may find yourself with a lot of “prescriptions” to fill.

Serves: 8 people
Prep Time: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 1 hour
Calories: 61 calories

Ingredients:
  • 2 bone-in, skin-on chicken breasts, preferably with ribs attached
  • 8 cups water
  • 4 carrots, chopped medium
  • 2 parsnips, chopped medium
  • 2 ribs celery, chopped medium
  • 1 small yellow onion, chopped small
  • 1 teaspoon fresh thyme, or ½ teaspoon dried
  • Salt
  • 1 bay leaf
  • 3 tablespoons minced fresh parsley
Instructions:

  1. Heat the 8-quart Stock Pot over medium heat until it’s hot enough that water droplets bead across the surface, about 2 minutes.
  2. Place the chicken breasts skin-side down in the hot, dry pot and cook until the chicken comes away from the bottom of the pan with no resistance and the skin is nicely browned, about 6 minutes. Transfer the chicken to a plate and set aside.
  3. Add the water, carrots, parsnips, celery, onion, thyme, ¾ teaspoon salt, and bay leaf. Stir to combine, scraping up any browned bits. Remove and discard the chicken skin and return the breasts to the pot.
  4. Cover and cook over medium heat until steam just begins to escape from under the lid, about 5 minutes.
  5. Spin the lid to engage the vapor seal then immediately reduce the heat to low. Cook until the chicken is cooked through and the vegetables are tender, about 45 minutes. (After about 10 minutes give the lid a quick spin—if it spins easily, leave it alone until it’s done. If not, increase the heat to re-engage the water seal then reduce the heat medium-low and continue cooking as directed.)
  6. Remove the pot from the heat. Transfer the chicken to a plate and set aside until cool enough to handle. Pull the meat from the bones and shred or cut into bite-sized pieces. Stir the chicken and parsley into the soup and season with salt if needed. Heat over low heat until the chicken in warmed through. Serve.
articles.author: Brittany Pitschman

articles.title: Apple Chutney
articles.body:
Chutneys are chunky and spicy. They compliment meat dishes adding a sweet and sour bite.

Serves: 4 
Calories:196 calories


Ingredients:

  • 2-large apples, peeled, cored and cut into 1” chunks (Gala or any sweet apple)
  • (This should yield about 3 ½ cups of apple chunks)
  • ½ cup of golden raisins
  • 1/3 cup of brown sugar
  • ¼ cup of water
  • 2 Tablespoons of Sherry Vinegar
  • ½ teaspoon candied (crystallized) ginger, finely chopped
  • 4 whole allspice berries
  • ¼ teaspoon coarse salt
  • Pinch of freshly ground black pepper
  • Pinch of freshly grated nutmeg


Instructions:
  1. Combine and stir all the ingredients in the 360 by Americraft 2-quart saucepan. Cover the pan and place over medium heat. 
  2. Cook until steam just begins to escape from under the lid. (5-7 minutes) Spin the lid to engage the Vapor Seal. Immediately reduce the heat to low, continue cooking for 30 minutes.
  3. Uncover the saucepan and raise the heat to medium-low. Allow the chutney to simmer until the liquid has reduced and takes on a syrupy consistency.
  4. Taste and adjust seasonings. Serve warm or chilled.

***Tip: Our Apple Chutney goes well with the Achiote-Rubbed Pork Chops.
articles.author: Brittany Pitschman

articles.title: Blueberry Cobbler

image.altText: Close-up of blueberry cobbler in a white ramekin topped with whipped cream and a mint leaf, spoon at the side on a light plate

articles.body:
This juicy dessert is as easy as 1-2-3

Serves: 6 people
Prep Time: 5 minutes
Cooking Time: 25 minutes
Calories: 230 calories

Ingredients:

  • 12 ounces fresh blueberries or frozen blueberries
  • 1 cup chopped fresh pineapple, or 1 (8-ounce) can unsweetened crushed pineapple with juice
  • 1 (9-ounce) box organic or natural plain or lemon-flavored muffin or cake mix
  • 1 teaspoon cinnamon



Instructions:

  1. Combine the blueberries and pineapple in the 3 Quart Sauce Pan. 
  2. Whisk together the muffin mix and 1 teaspoon cinnamon in a bowl. Sprinkle the mixture evenly over the fruit.
  3. Cover the pot and cook over medium heat until steam just begins to escape from the lid, about 5 minutes.
  4. Spin the lid to engage the vapor seal, then immediately reduce the heat to low. Cook for about 20 minutes or until the fruit is bubbly and the topping is firm to the touch.
articles.author: Brittany Pitschman

articles.title: Braised Cabbage Rolls
articles.body:
This one-pot dinner is definitely a “Grandmamma” recipe. It takes a little time but will transport you to an “old-timey” place of comfort and warmth. Thanks Grandma!


Serves: 16 people
Prep Time: 1 hour, 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 2 hours
Calories: 201 calories


Ingredients:

  • 1-3 lb. head of Savoy or regular cabbage
  • 2 cups of water
  • ½ teaspoon kosher salt


Meat Filling:

  • 1 lb. ground beef
  • ½ lb. ground pork
  • ½ lb. ground lamb
  • ½ cup uncooked long grain brown rice
  • ½ sweet onion finely chopped
  • 2 cloves garlic minced
  • 2 teaspoons toasted caraway seeds
  • kosher salt
  • Freshly ground black pepper

Tomato Sauce:

  • 28 oz. can San Marzano whole tomatoes (puree in food mill or processor)
  • 2 cups low sodium, bottled vegetable juice
  • 1½ cups of water
  • 2 Tablespoons granulated sugar
  • 2 Tablespoons light brown sugar
  • 1/3 cup of apple cider vinegar
  • ½ teaspoon salt
  • 1/8 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper


Instructions:

  1. Wash and core the head of cabbage leaving the rest of the head intact.
  2. Place 2-cups of water and ½ teaspoon kosher salt in the 360 by Americraft 8-quart stockpot. Place the cabbage, core side down in the stockpot. Cover the pot with the lid.
  3. Cook over medium heat just until vapor begins to escape from under the lid. (Approximately 5 minutes) Spin the lid to engage the vapor seal. Immediately reduce the heat to low. Cook for 7-8 minutes
  4. Remove lid. Gently peel back leaves from cabbage head using tongs. Leaves should separate easily. Use care not to tear the cabbage leaves. (These are your meat filling wrappers.) Place each leaf in a colander to cool. (You should be able to get 16-20 leaves.) Remove remainder of cabbage head to cool.
  5. Reserve 1 ½ cups of the cabbage liquid. Return the liquid to the empty stockpot and add ½ cup uncooked long grain brown rice. Stir once. Replace the lid.
  6. Cook the rice on medium heat just until steam begins to escape from under the lid.
  7. (3-5 minutes) Spin the lid to engage the vapor seal. Immediately reduce the heat to low. Cook the rice about 40 minutes; rice should be tender.
  8. Remove the pan from the heat. If there’s any excess liquid, pour the rice through a strainer. Transfer rice to a bowl to cool. .
  9. Combine beef, pork, lamb, cooled rice, onion, garlic, and toasted caraway seeds. Season the mixture with kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste.
  10. Trim tough center stem from each cabbage leaf. 
  11. Slice thinly the remaining cabbage head. Line the bottom of the 360 by Americraft
  12. 8-quart stockpot with the sliced cabbage.
  13. Assemble rolls by laying the cabbage leaves out flat. Place 2 Tablespoons of meat mixture at the bottom of each leaf. Fold the bottom sides of the cabbage over the meat. Roll up and fold sides of leaf inward. Continue to roll up entire cabbage leaf to make a little bundle. (Like a burrito)
  14. Stack all your cabbage bundles, seam side down in the stockpot on top of the sliced cabbage.
  15. Mix together in a large bowl, the pureed tomatoes, vegetable juice, water, sugars, vinegar, salt, and pepper. Carefully pour liquid over cabbage bundles.
  16. Invert a heatproof plate as a weight on top of the bundles. (This should prevent them from coming unraveled during the cooking process.)
  17. Cover the pot with the lid. Cook over medium heat just until steam begins to escape from under the lid. (Approximately 20 minutes) Spin the lid to engage the vapor seal. Immediately reduce the heat to low. Cook the cabbage rolls for 30 minutes.
  18. Remove the lid. Return the heat to medium. Allow the pot to simmer to reduce the amount of liquid and thicken the sauce. (45 minutes-1 hour)
  19. Carefully remove hot plate. (Use tongs to lift the edge of the plate then remove plate wearing waterproof oven mitts.)
  20. Serve with German spaetzel or mashed potatoes, and roasted fall root vegetables.


**Timesaver Tip: While your rice is cooking you can get your cabbage, onion, and garlic chopped. There’s even time to combine the tomato sauce ingredients.

articles.title: Frittata
articles.body:
In Spain they are called tortillas, in Italy this egg dish is named the Frittata. Served for breakfast, lunch or dinner this pan omelet is versatile and easy to prepare. Serve it right from the pan with buttered toast or a side salad.

Serves: 8 people
Calories: 118 calories


Ingredients:
  • 10 whole eggs, large
  • ¼ cup of cream or milk
  • 2-Tablespoons grated Romano or Parmesan cheese
  • 1-cup of potato cut into small dice
  • 1-cup of sliced white or crimini mushrooms
  • 1/3 cup of purple onion cut into small dice
  • ¼ cup of sweet red bell pepper cut into small dice
  • ½ teaspoon of de-stemmed thyme leaves
  • ½ cup fresh spinach roughly chopped
  • Coarse salt
  • Freshly ground black pepper

Instructions:
  1. Whip the eggs together in a large bowl. Add the cream and grated cheese. Stir to combine. Set aside under refrigeration.
  2. Pre-heat the 360 by Americraft large fry pan over medium heat. 
  3. Add 2-Tablespoons of butter to the pan and allow it to melt.
  4. Add the potatoes, mushrooms, onion, bell pepper and thyme leaves to the pan. Season the ingredients with salt and pepper to taste. Sauté everything over medium heat until the potatoes are tender, approximately 10 minutes. (If anything sticks to the pan, deglaze it by adding 2 tablespoons of water then scrape the bottom of the pan. Continue cooking until water has evaporated.)
  5. Remove the egg mixture from the refrigerator. Re-whip the ingredients then add the chopped spinach. Pour this mixture over the vegetables in the fry pan. Give the mixture a few seconds to begin to set, and then gently scrape the bottom of the pan with a wooden spoon. You are moving the eggs around, not to scramble them but to allow the bottom to cook evenly. Repeat this procedure until the eggs become slightly firm.
  6. Preheat your broiler. Place the fry pan on the top rack of the oven close to the broiler. The eggs will begin to puff up and become set in the pan. When the frittata is firm but still moist, remove the pan from under the heat. Allow it to sit for a minute or two before serving.

*Variation: Add ½ cup of chopped ham, bacon or cooked meat of your choice.

articles.title: Great Northern Bean Soup with Crispy Pancetta
articles.body:
If you love soup, this will warm your heart and belly. Pancetta is an Italian, uncured bacon that adds a salty bite and crispy texture. I’ve used both the 4-quart and 6-quart stockpots depending on whether I’m feeding a few or a few more! Here are the instructions for the larger batch.

Serves: 8 people
Calories: 337 calories


Ingredients:
  • 8-ounces of pancetta chopped into small dice
  • 3-Tablespoons of olive oil, divided into 1-Tablespoon and 2-Tablespoon portions
  • 2-cups of Spanish onion chopped into small dice
  • 1-cup of celery chopped into small dice
  • 1-cup carrot chopped into small dice
  • 1-pound Great Northern or Navy beans (That have been soaked in cold water overnight, then drained)
  • 4-cups vegetable stock or chicken stock
  • 3-cups water
  • 2 sprigs of fresh thyme
  • 2 bay leaves
  • Coarse salt
  • Freshly ground black pepper

Instructions:
  1. Preheat the 360 by Americraft 6-quart stockpot over medium heat for 1-2 minutes.
  2. Add one tablespoon of olive oil. Allow it to heat for a minute. Add 8-ounces of chopped pancetta to the pan. You’ll hear it sizzle. Let the meat brown and cook for
  3. 4 minutes before turning. (Be patient, the meat will release from the pan easily after it’s cooked for a bit.) Stir the pancetta and cook until it’s brown and crispy. (About 8 minutes)
  4. Transfer the pancetta to a paper towel-lined plate to drain. Pour off and discard any excess fat in the pot but keep the crispy brown bits at the bottom. This is called the fond.
  5. Return the stockpot to medium heat. Add 2-tablespoons of olive oil. Allow it to heat for a minute. Add the onion, celery, and carrot. Stir to coat the vegetables with the oil. As you stir, scrape up all the fond from the bottom of the pot. Cook the vegetables for 12-15 minutes.
  6. Do not season the vegetables yet. Bean cookery is slightly different than other soups. Adding salt at this stage will make the beans tough. We’ll season everything towards the end of the cooking process.
  7. Add the drained beans, thyme sprigs, and bay leaves to the pot. Pour in the stock and the water. Bring the mixture to a boil.
  8. Cover the pot. Continue cooking until steam just begins to escape from under the lid. Spin the lid to engage the Vapor seal. Immediately reduce the heat to low.
  9. Cook the soup for one hour. Check to make sure the beans are tender. If they are not, continue cooking a few minutes more.
  10. Remove the lid when beans are tender. Transfer one-quarter of the beans and vegetables along with some broth to a food processor bowl with the blade attachment. Pulse the mixture into a puree. Return the puree to the stockpot.
  11. Add three-fourths of the cooked pancetta. (Reserve the remainder) Season the soup with coarse salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste.
  12. Cover the pot and let the soup simmer on low heat for another 30 minutes.
  13. Remove the lid. Remove and discard the thyme sprigs and bay leaves. Stir, taste and adjust the final seasonings.

**Tip: Sprinkle a bit of the reserved pancetta on top of each bowl of soup just before serving.

articles.title: This Little Piggy Pulled Pork
articles.author: Brittany Pitschman

recipekitMetafields.value:
{"recipe_title":"This Little Piggy Pulled Pork","recipe_author":"

360 Cookware

","recipe_description":"

Cookware Items Used In This Recipe:

  • 8 Quart and Cover
  • Large Cookie Sheet


Here’s a recipe for easy and delicious pulled pork that takes only a few hours to cook. Marinate the pork for at least 24 hours but 2-3 days yields even better results. The meat can be used in tamales, enchiladas and of course for pulled pork sandwiches. Look for our "I’m Goin’ to Kansas City Barbecue Sauce" recipe here on the 360 Cookware web site.

","recipe_category":"Breakfast & Lunch","recipe_cuisine":null,"recipe_ingredients":[{"type":"heading","ingredient":"blank","heading_text":"Marinade Ingredients"},{"ingredient":"

1-cup of vegetable oil

","selected_product":null},{"ingredient":"

½ cup of apple cider vinegar

"},{"ingredient":"

6-cloves of garlic

"},{"ingredient":"

2-Tablespoons of coarse salt

"},{"ingredient":"

2-Tablespoons of the Spice Mix

"},{"ingredient":"

1-Tablespoon Worcestershire sauce

"},{"ingredient":"

Juice from one lime

"},{"type":"heading","ingredient":"blank","heading_text":"Spice Mix"},{"ingredient":"

2-Tablespoons of black peppercorns

"},{"ingredient":"

2-Tablespoons of dried oregano

"},{"ingredient":"

1-teaspoon whole Allspice

"}],"recipe_directions":[{"id":1742573150928.221,"type":"heading","direction":"blank","heading_text":"Preparing The Meat"},{"id":1742573150928.034,"direction":"

Clean and pat dry the pork shoulder.

"},{"id":1742573150928.5178,"direction":"

Score the skin in a crosshatch fashion.

"},{"id":1742573150928.8354,"direction":"

Set aside.

"},{"id":1742573150928.623,"type":"heading","direction":"blank","heading_text":"Marinade"},{"id":1742573150928.9604,"direction":"

Grind the 3 ingredients for the Spice Mix in a spice grinder. You will need 2 tablespoons of this spice mix for the marinade. Store the rest in an airtight container for up to 1 year.

"},{"id":1742573150928.888,"direction":"

Pulse the garlic, salt, 2 Tablespoons of the Spice Mix, Worcestershire sauce, and lime juice in a food processor bowl fitted with the blade attachment.

"},{"id":1742573150928.7715,"direction":"

Add the apple cider vinegar to the bowl.

"},{"id":1742573150928.0713,"direction":"

Turn the processor on and drizzle in the vegetable oil to form an emulsion.

"},{"id":1742573150928.575,"direction":"

Place the pork shoulder in a 2-gallon re-sealable plastic bag.

"},{"id":1742573150928.4539,"direction":"

Pour the marinade mix into the bag over the meat.

"},{"id":1742573150928.0537,"direction":"

Seal the bag removing as much air as possible.

"},{"id":1742573150928.2588,"direction":"

Place the bag on a baking sheet and move the marinade around to entirely coat the meat.

"},{"id":1742573150928.1973,"direction":"

Place everything under refrigeration.

"},{"id":1742573150928.9841,"direction":"

During the next day or so turn the pork shoulder a few times to redistribute the marinade.

"},{"id":1742573150928.181,"direction":"

Keep the meat under refrigeration for at least 24 hours and up to three days.

"},{"id":1742573150928.2917,"type":"heading","direction":"blank","heading_text":"When you're ready to begin the cooking process"},{"id":1742573150928.192,"direction":"

Remove the pork shoulder from the refrigerator and allow it to rest at room temperature for 30 minutes.

"},{"id":1742573150928.7454,"direction":"

Slice one large onion (white or yellow) into thin rings.

"},{"id":1742573150928.1958,"direction":"

Place the sliced onion in your 8 Quart Stockpot.

"},{"id":1742573150928.8618,"direction":"

Pour ½ cup of water over the onions.

"},{"id":1742573150928.236,"direction":"

Remove the pork shoulder from the plastic bag.

"},{"id":1742573150928.7612,"direction":"

Discard the excess marinade.

"},{"id":1742573150928.29,"direction":"

Place the pork shoulder on top of the onions.

"},{"id":1742573150928.3052,"direction":"

Cover the pot and place it over medium heat.

"},{"id":1742573150928.0056,"direction":"

Cook until steam just begins to escape from under the lid.

"},{"id":1742573150928.2156,"direction":"

Spin the lid to engage the Vapor Seal.

"},{"id":1742573150928.6338,"direction":"

Immediately reduce the heat to low.

"},{"id":1742573150928.1094,"direction":"

Cook the pork shoulder for 3 ½ hours.

"},{"id":1742573150928.0579,"direction":"

Check the amount of broth in the pot after three hours. There should be plenty of liquid, if not, add another ½ cup of water and replace the lid. If liquid is added, increase the heat to medium until steam begins to escape from under the lid.

"},{"id":1742573150928.9666,"direction":"

Spin the lid to engage the Vapor Seal and reduce heat to low.

"},{"id":1742573150928.9297,"direction":"

Remove the pot from the heat and allow it to rest covered for ½ an hour.

"},{"id":1742573150928.0984,"direction":"

Uncover the pot and carefully transfer the meat to a Large Cookie Sheet.

"},{"id":1742573150928.4695,"direction":"

Pour the broth into a separate container. (Don’t throw it out. There’s lots of flavor in it.)

"},{"id":1742573150928.7305,"direction":"

Separate the meat from the bone once it becomes just cool enough to handle.

"},{"id":1742573150928.2651,"direction":"

“Pull” the pork to separate the strands of meat from one another.

"},{"id":1742573150928.4993,"direction":"

Continue this until you’ve gone through all the meat.

"},{"id":1742573150928.8608,"direction":"

Discard the excess fat and bone.

"},{"id":1742573150928.2917,"direction":"

Cool both the meat and the broth or use some right away.

"}],"serving_size":"6","prep_time":null,"cook_time":null,"recipe_image":"https://f000.backblazeb2.com/file/recipekit-bucket/v1602250097_this-little-piggy-pulled-pork-_ecdfdt.jpg","recipe_image_alt_text":"Pulled Pork sliders","iso_prep_time":null,"iso_cook_time":null,"recipe_rating":"4.0000000000000000","enable_rating":true,"rating_count":"10","recipe_note":"

Tip: This is a great recipe to make ahead of time. The pork freezes beautifully. Portion it into quart size freezer bags once its been pulled.

Tip: Chill the broth for several hours then remove the top layer of fat. The broth can be used for soups but I like to add some of it back into the pork for added flavor and moisture.

Hint: Use care not to puncture the marination bag with the pork bone.

Comment: This recipe is three steps: marinate the meat, cook it, and then “pull” the meat to form pulled pork. Check out this recipe from the 360 Vapor® Cooks Better Cookbook.

articles.title: Easy Double Chocolate Skillet Cake

image.altText: A slice of double chocolate skillet cake on a white plate with a spoon and a cup of coffee in the background.

articles.summary:
360 Cookware Used: 3.5 Quart Sauté Pan w/Cover Easy Double Chocolate Skillet Cake   Save Print Prep time 20 mins Cook time 65 mins Total time 1 hour 25 mins   This super-moist and chocolaty cake looks and tastes as if you spent the whole day slaving in the kitchen but the truth is it comes... 

 

Read More »
articles.body:
This super-moist and chocolaty cake looks and tastes as if you spent the whole day slaving in the kitchen but the truth is it comes together as easily as a quick bread and “bakes” on top of the stove. We like it warm with ice cream for an easy weeknight treat or dressed up with luscious chocolate sauce and dollops of fresh whipped cream.

Prep time: 20 mins
Cook time: 65 mins
Total time: 1 hour 25 mins
Author: 360 Cookware
, opens in a new tab. Opens in a new windowServes: 10
3.5 Quart Sauté Pan w/Cover

Ingredients:
  • Non stick cooking spray
  • 4 ounces unsweetened chocolate, melted and cooled
  • 1½ cups all-purpose flour
  • 1½ cups sugar
  • ½ cup Dutch-processed cocoa powder
  • 1½ teaspoons baking powder
  • 1 teaspoons baking soda
  • 1 teaspoon salt
  • 1½ cups buttermilk
  • 2 teaspoons instant espresso powder or instant coffee granules
  • ½ cup vegetable oil
  • 2 large eggs, at room temperature
Instructions:
  1. Spray the 3.5 Quart Sauté PanOpens in a new window with non-stick cooking spray and set aside.
  2. Combine the flour, sugar, cocoa powder, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl and whisk to combine.
  3. In another bowl, whisk the buttermilk and espresso powder together until the coffee granules are dissolved.
  4. Whisk the oil and eggs into the buttermilk mixture.
  5. Whisk the buttermilk mixture into the flour mixture until just combined.
  6. Whisk in the melted chocolate until the batter is a uniform color with no streaks of flour or chocolate.
  7. Scrape the batter into the prepared skillet and smooth it out to the edges of the pan.
  8. Cover and cook over low heat until the edges are cooked and the center is set, 45 to 65 minutes. (You will need to gently touch the cake with your fingers. It will feel undercooked in the middle, but it shouldn’t be goopy.)
  9. Replace the cover and move the pan off-heat. Allow to stand for 5 min.
  10. Uncover and let stand for about 5 minutes until the surface of the cake is dry.
  11. Place a cooling rack over the skillet and invert the cake onto the rack.
  12. Serve warm or cool completely. Dust with powdered sugar and serve.

articles.body:
Ingredients:
  • 3 ½ pounds of sweet potatoes (4 large)
  • 4 ounces of unsalted butter (1 stick, cut into 8 tablespoon size pieces)
  • ½ cup of evaporated milk
  • ½ cup of lightly packed light brown sugar
  • Pinch of coarse salt
  • 1-10.5 ounce package of miniature marshmallows
Instructions:
  1. Wash the potatoes, pierce their skins with a fork, and place them in the
  2. 360 by Americraft 4-quart stockpot. Add 1/3 cup of water to the pot. Cover the pot and place over medium heat.
  3. Cook the potatoes until steam just begins to escape from under the lid. Spin the lid to engage the Vapor Seal. Immediately reduce the heat to low. Continue cooking until the potatoes can be easily pierced with a fork. (50 minutes) Remove the pot from the heat and allow it to rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
  4. Transfer the potatoes to a baking sheet. Allow them to cool for 10 minutes. Pierce the skins with a fork. Using the fork, tear the skins away from the potatoes. The peels should easily fall away.
  5. Mash the potatoes in a large bowl with a potato masher. Leave them slightly chunky. Stir in the butter, evaporated milk, brown sugar, and salt. Stir to melt the butter and combine everything well. (This should yield 6-7 cups of mixed sweet potatoes)
  6. Spray the 360 by Americraft 2.3-quart casserole lightly with vegetable spray.
  7. Layer evenly, ½ of the sweet potato mixture in the bottom of the casserole. Layer ½ of the marshmallows on top of the potatoes. Spread the remainder of the sweet potatoes as the third layer.
  8. Cover the casserole and place the pan on the 360 Slow Cooker Base preheated to 2 ½. Cook the casserole until everything is heated through. (30-40 minutes)
  9. Uncover the casserole and top it with the final layer of marshmallows. Turn on your broiler. Place the casserole on the center rack of the oven under the broiler. Do not leave this unattended. The marshmallows will toast quickly.
  10. (Approximately 3 minutes) Rotate the pan to evenly toast all the marshmallows.
  11. Remove the casserole from under the broiler. Return it, uncovered, to the slow cooker base to keep it warm. Reduce slow cooker base temperature to a 1 setting.

articles.title: Vegetable Stacks with Mozzarella and Basil

image.altText: Vegetable stacks of zucchini, roasted red pepper, and mozzarella simmering in marinara in a 360 Cookware stainless sauté pan

articles.body:
Ingredients:
  • 2 medium zucchini, cut into ¼-inch rounds
  • 2 to 3 jarred roasted red peppers, seeds removed, and cut into approximately 2-inch by 2-inch pieces,
  • 8 ounces fresh mozzarella, thinly sliced, and cut into approximately 2-inch by 2-inch pieces
  • ½ cup prepared pesto
  • 1 ½ cups 360 Marinara Sauce
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper
  • Toothpicks
Instructions:
  1. Toss the zucchini with salt and pepper.
  2. To build stacks place one piece of zucchini on a cutting board or cookie sheet and spread with a thin layer of pesto.
  3. Cover the pesto with a piece of the mozzarella, followed by a piece of roasted pepper, a piece of zucchini, another thin layer of pesto, and a piece of roasted pepper. Finish the stack with a piece of mozzarella.
  4. Repeat with remaining vegetables, pesto, and cheese. Secure each stack with a toothpick at opposite ends.
  5. Pour the marinara sauce into the 3.5 Quart Sauté Pan.
  6. Carefully arrange the stacks in the pan about an inch apart on top of the sauce.
  7. Cover and cook over medium heat until steam just begins to escape from under the lid, about 5 minutes.
  8. Spin the lid to engage the vapor seal then immediately reduce the heat to low. Cook for 1 minute.
  9. Remove the pan from the heat and let stand for 10 to 12 minutes until the vegetables are tender and the cheese is melted.
  10. To serve remove the toothpicks and divide stacks among small plates. Spoon the sauce around each portion and garnish with a dollop of pesto. Serve.

articles.title: Garden Fresh Vegetable Soup
articles.body:
The beauty of this soup--aside from the garden-fresh flavors and quick cooking—is how easily it adapts to suit the seasons. Replace the canned tomatoes with vine-ripened tomatoes and some sweet, tender green beans or fresh peas in summer, or swap the kale for a combination of your favorite hearty greens, once the air turns crisp. Add a cup of short pasta along with the beans for a truly soul-warming winter soup.

Serves: 6 to 8
Prep Time: 30 Minutes
Cooking Time: 45 Minutes
Cookware: 8-quart Stockpot

Ingredients:

  • 1 tablespoon extra virgin olive oil, plus more for garnish
  • 1 large onion, chopped medium
  • 2 carrots, chopped medium
  • 1 bulb fennel, trimmed and chopped medium
  • 2 garlic cloves, minced
  • Salt
  • 4 cups low-sodium chicken broth or water
  • 1 (28 ounce) can diced tomatoes with their juice
  • 1 (19 ounce) can cannellini beans or chickpeas, rinsed and drained
  • 1 bunch kale, or Swiss chard, stems removed, leaves washed and coarsely chopped
  • 1 zucchini, diced medium
  • 1 yellow squash, diced medium
  • 1 red or yellow bell pepper, seeded and diced medium
  • Freshly ground black pepper
  • Freshly grated Parmesan cheese

Instructions: 

  1. Heat 8-quart Stockpot over medium heat for 1 minute. Add olive oil onions, carrots, fennel, garlic, and season with salt. Cook the vegetables for about 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they are softened.
  2. Stir in the broth, tomatoes, beans, kale, zucchini, squash, and bell pepper, and season with black pepper.
  3. Cover and cook over medium heat until steam just begins to escape from under the lid, about 5 minutes. 
  4. Spin the lid to engage the vapor seal then immediately reduce the heat to low. Cook until the vegetables are tender, 20 to 30 minutes. (After about 10 minutes give the lid a quick spin—if it spins easily, leave it alone until it’s done. If not, increase the heat to re-engage the water seal then reduce the heat to medium-low and continue cooking as directed.)

"},{"direction":"

Add the 2 cups of butternut squash and thyme leaves. Season everything with coarse salt and pepper. Stir and continue cooking for 10 minutes.

"},{"direction":"

Add 1 cup of Arborio rice to the pan. Stir the rice to toast it in the pan for 2 minutes. Stir, stir, then stir some more. This will prevent burning.

"},{"direction":"

Add 1 cup of stock to the pan. Stir gently until the stock is absorbed. Add another cup of stock and stir until it has been absorbed. Taste the broth and season the dish with salt.

"},{"direction":"

Repeat the addition of stock but reduce the amount to ½ cup with each addition. Be sure the stock has been absorbed before adding more. Taste and season frequently. You’ll need to layer in the salt a little at a time.

"},{"direction":"

Continue to add stock, stir, taste, and season the risotto until you’ve used all the stock or the rice will absorb no more liquid.

"},{"direction":"

Remove the pan from the heat and transfer to a serving dish.

articles.title: Mussels with White Wine-Herb Broth
articles.body:
This dish is all about the fresh herbs—and lots of them. Serve with slabs of toasted country bread for dipping into the herbaceous broth.

Serves: 4 (appetizer)
Serves: 2 (main dish)
Prep Time Serves: 15 minutes
Cooking Time: 25-30 minutes

Ingredients:

  • 4 cups boiling water 
  • 2 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil 
  • 2 large shallots, minced 
  • 4 garlic cloves, minced 
  • Salt 
  • 2 pounds mussels, beards removed 
  • 2 cups dry white wine or vermouth 
  • 1 tablespoon chopped fresh thyme 
  • 1 bay leaf 
  • ¼ cup chopped fresh parsley 
  • 2 tablespoons chopped fresh tarragon or basil 
  • Freshly ground black pepper

Instructions:

  1. Pour the boiling water into a large serving bowl and set aside to warm while preparing the mussels.
  2. Heat the oil in the 4-Quart Stock Pot.
  3. Add the shallots, and garlic and season with a little salt. Cook for about 4 minutes, stirring often, until soft. 
  4. Add the mussels, wine, thyme, and bay leaf.
  5. Cover and cook until steam just begins to escape from under the lid.
  6. Spin the lid to engage the vapor seal then immediately reduce the heat to low. Cook for 4 minutes. Lift the lid and give the mussels a quick, but gentle stir. If the mussels are not open, replace the lid and cook for another 15. (Do not over cook or they will be crumbly and tough.)
  7. Discard the hot water from the bowl. Use a slotted spoon to transfer the mussels to the warm bowl. Discard any unopened mussels. Cover loosely with foil.
  8. Stir the parsley and tarragon into the broth and season with salt and a few grinds of pepper.
  9. Pour the broth over the mussels and serve immediately.

articles.title: Southern Banh Mi Tacos
articles.body:
Ingredients: 

Sriracha Spread

  • 1 cup mayonnaise 
  • 4 teaspoons prepared horseradish  
  • 4 teaspoons Worcestershire sauce
  • 4 teaspoons soy sauce 
  • 2 tablespoons plus 2 teaspoons Sriracha hot chili sauce
  • 1/2 teaspoon fresh lime juice

 Seared Beef Tips

  • 1 (3-pound) chuck roast
  • 2 ½ teaspoons fine sea salt
  • ¾ teaspoon cracked black pepper
  • 3 cloves garlic, chopped
  • ½ yellow onion, sliced
  • 1/2 cup beef stock
  • 2 teaspoons olive or canola oil

 Carrot-Broccoli Slaw

  • 6 tablespoons rice vinegar
  • 2 tablespoons sugar
  • pinch fine sea salt
  • 3 or 4 medium carrots
  • 3 or 4 broccoli stalks

 Tacos

  • 12 corn tortillas
  • ½ fresh jalapeno pepper, thinly sliced
  • 1/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves

Instructions:

  1. For the Sriracha Spread, combine the mayonnaise, horseradish, Worcestershire sauce, soy sauce, Sriracha and lime juice in a small bowl. Whisk until smooth. Use immediately or refrigerate for up to 1 week. (Makes about 1 cup)
  2. For the Seared Beef Tips, remove any large pieces of fat from the roast. Do not discard. Cut the beef into about 1-inch cubes, and place them in the 360 Cookware Slow Cooker.
  3. Add the salt, pepper, and garlic. Place the sliced onion on top of the beef, then position the fat pieces over the onions. Pour in the beef stock.
  4. Cover and place on base. Simmer at setting #3 for about 5 hours or until meat is fork tender but doesn’t fall apart. Discard the fat and onions. Using a slotted spoon, carefully remove the cubes of beef from the pot and transfer to a bowl. Allow to cool for 30 minutes.
  5. Heat an 8.5” 360 Cookware Fry Pan over medium heat. Add 1 teaspoon of the oil, and swirl the pan to coat the bottom. With paper towels, pat the cubed beef dry, and then add some to the pan. Work in batches to avoid overcrowding the pan. Cook until seared on all sides, tossing occasionally. Transfer to a serving dish. Add the remaining 1 teaspoon canola oil, and cook the remaining beef.
  6. For the Slaw, combine the vinegar, sugar, and salt in a medium microwave-safe bowl. Microwave for 1 minute. Stir until sugar dissolves. Cool in the refrigerator. Meanwhile, position the #2 stringer cone on the 360 Kitchen Cutter. Feed the carrots and broccoli through the cutter to create julienne strips. Add the vegetables to the vinaigrette. Toss with tongs to combine.
  7. For the Tacos, warm the tortillas in the microwave for 30 seconds to 1 minute or until warm. To assemble, place some of the seared beef tips in each tortilla and then top with the Sriracha spread, carrot-broccoli slaw, jalapeno slices and cilantro.

Serves 4 (3 tacos).

Recipe Created By: Whitney Miller 

Recipe adapted from New Southern Table.

Cookware Items Used In This Recipe:

  • 8-Quart Stock Pot

","recipe_category":"Entreés","recipe_cuisine":null,"recipe_ingredients":[{"ingredient":"

1-10 pound whole turkey

","selected_product":null},{"ingredient":"

1-cup white onion chopped into small dice

"},{"ingredient":"

1/2-cup celery chopped into small dice

"},{"ingredient":"

1/2-cup carrot chopped into small dice

"},{"ingredient":"

Fresh parsley (2-teaspoons finely chopped plus 3 whole sprigs)

"},{"ingredient":"

Fresh thyme (1-teaspoon finely chopped thyme leaves plus 3 whole sprigs)

"},{"ingredient":"

Fresh sage (½ -teaspoon finely chopped plus 2 whole sprigs)

"},{"ingredient":"

Fresh rosemary (½ -teaspoon finely chopped plus 2 whole sprigs)

"},{"ingredient":"

Browning and seasoning sauce (found in the spice aisle of your grocery store)

"},{"ingredient":"

4-ounces unsalted butter (softened)

"},{"ingredient":"

2 Tablespoons all-purpose flour

"},{"ingredient":"

Coarse salt

"},{"ingredient":"

Freshly ground black pepper

"}],"recipe_directions":[{"type":"heading","direction":"blank","heading_text":"Herb Butter"},{"direction":"

Soften one stick (4 ounces) of butter and place it in a medium bowl. Add the chopped parsley, thyme, sage, and rosemary to the bowl and mix to incorporate. Reserve half of the mixture to prepare the turkey. Place the other half of the butter in the center of a piece of plastic wrap. Roll the wrap over the butter and twist both ends tightly to form a cylinder. (…as salt-water taffy is wrapped) Place the rolled butter in the freezer for thirty minutes to set. (4 Tablespoons of herb butter are needed for the gravy.) You may store this in a sealed freezer bag in the refrigerator for 2 weeks or in the freezer for up to six months.

"},{"direction":"

Clean and pat the turkey dry. Be certain to remove the giblets and neck from the cavities of the bird. Without tearing, use your hands to just separate the skin from both sides of the breast. Rub the herb butter under the skin to coat the meat. Use the butter left on your hands to coat all of the outside skin. Wash your hands. Liberally salt and pepper all sides of the turkey including the cavity. Stuff the cavity with the herb sprigs. Fold the wings underneath the neck. Secure the legs with butcher’s twine or tuck them into the pierced skin flap at the tailbone. Wash your hands.

"},{"direction":"

Cover the bottom of the 8-quart stock

pot with ¾ of the chopped onion, celery, and carrot. (Reserve the remaining ¼ of the vegetables to cook the giblets.) Season the vegetables with a pinch of salt and freshly ground pepper. Add ½ cup of water. Place the turkey on top of the vegetables.

"},{"direction":"

Cover the pot and place it over medium heat. Cook until steam just begins to escape from under the lid (about 15 minutes). Spin the lid to engage the Vapor Seal. Immediately reduce the heat to low.

"},{"direction":"

Uncover the pot after 45 minutes. Using a silicone or pastry brush, baste the turkey with the browning and seasoning sauce. This will help flavor the skin and achieve a nice golden brown color. Cover the pot and continue cooking. Baste the turkey after another 20 minutes. After two bastings with the browning and seasoning sauce, additional bastings should include the juices from the pot to moisten the bird.

"},{"direction":"

Check the temperature of the turkey after 1 hour and 30 minutes of cooking by inserting a thermometer into the thigh without touching the bone. Any juices should be clear. The temperature should read 165 degrees Fahrenheit. If the bird hasn’t reached this temperature, baste the bird again and replace the cover.   Cook another few minutes. When the turkey reaches the desired temperature, remove the pot from the heat and allow it to rest, uncovered for 10-15 minutes.

"},{"direction":"

Transfer the turkey to a serving platter. Use caution, as there will be hot juices in the cavity of the bird.

"},{"direction":"

Strain the broth and reserve it to make gravy in the same pot.

"},{"type":"heading","direction":"blank","heading_text":"Cooking The Giblets"},{"direction":"

Place the remaining onion, celery, and carrot mixture in the bottom of the 1-quart saucepan. Add ¼ cup of water. Place the giblets and neck on top of the vegetables. Season everything with salt and pepper. You may add some sprigs of parsley, sage, rosemary, and thyme for additional flavor.

"},{"direction":"

Place the covered saucepan over medium heat. Cook until steam just begins to escape from under the lid. Spin the lid to engage the Vapor Seal. Immediately reduce the heat to low.

"},{"direction":"

Cook for 10 minutes. Remove the liver and heart if they have reached an internal temperature of 165 degrees Fahrenheit. Continue cooking the neck and kidneys for an additional 30 minutes.

"},{"direction":"

Remove the pan from the heat. Pick the meat from the neck and finely chop the giblets to add to the gravy, if desired.

"},{"type":"heading","direction":"blank","heading_text":"Turkey Gravy"},{"direction":"

Make a roux in the 8-quart stock pot by placing the pot over medium heat.

"},{"direction":"

Add 4 Tablespoons of the herb butter to the pan. Melt the butter. While whisking, sprinkle the flour over the melted butter. Continue whisking and cook for 3-4 minutes. This will cook out the flour taste. Heat the reserved broth and any additional liquid to be added. When the mixture is bubbly and pale, whisk in the broth reserved from the pot a little bit at a time. Bring the mixture to a boil. Adjust the consistency of the gravy by adding additional hot stock, water, even a bit of white wine (optional). Add the cooked giblets if desired. Heat everything to at least 165 degrees Fahrenheit. Salt and pepper to taste. Serve hot.

"}],"serving_size":null,"prep_time":null,"cook_time":null,"recipe_image":"https://f000.backblazeb2.com/file/recipekit-bucket/v1602732256_Food-0003_copy_ctb6wg.jpg","recipe_image_alt_text":null,"iso_prep_time":null,"iso_cook_time":null,"recipe_rating":"3.1290322580645161","enable_rating":true,"rating_count":"62","recipe_note":"

"},{"ingredient":"

½ cup of evaporated milk

Pinch of coarse salt

"},{"direction":"

"},{"direction":"

","selected_product":null},{"ingredient":"

"},{"ingredient":"

4 Carrots, chopped medium

"},{"ingredient":"

2 Parsnips, chopped medium

"},{"ingredient":"

"},{"ingredient":"

"}],"recipe_directions":[{"direction":"

Heat the 8 Quart Stock Pot over medium heat until it’s hot enough that water droplets bead across the surface, about 2 minutes.

"},{"direction":"

Place the chicken breasts skin-side down in the hot, dry pot and cook until the chicken comes away from the bottom of the pan with no resistance and the skin is nicely browned, about 6 minutes. Transfer the chicken to a plate and set aside.

"},{"direction":"

Add the water, carrots, parsnips, celery, onion, thyme, 3/4 teaspoon salt and bay leaf. Stir to combine, scraping up any browned bits. Remove and discard the chicken skin and return the breasts to the pot.

"},{"direction":"

Cover and cook over medium heat until steam begins to escape from under the lid, about 5 minutes.

"},{"direction":"

Spin the lid to engage the Vapor Seal then immediately reduce the heat to low. Cook until the chicken is cooked through and the vegetables are tender, about 45 minutes. (After about 10 minutes give the lid a quick spin. If it spins easily, leave it alone until it’s done. If not, increase the heat to re-engage the Vapor Seal then reduce the heat medium-low and continue cooking as directed.)

"},{"direction":"

Remove the pot from the heat. Transfer the chicken to a plate and set aside until cool enough to handle. Pull the meat from the bones and shred or cut into bite-sized pieces. Stir the chicken and parsley into the soup and season with salt if needed. Heat over low heat until the chicken is warmed through. Serve.

"},{"ingredient":"

Chef Emily Ellyn

","recipe_description":"

Cookware Items Used In This Recipe:

  • 4-Quart Stock Pot
  • Large Cookie Sheet
  • 2 quart Saucier Pan
","recipe_category":"Desserts & Breads","recipe_cuisine":null,"recipe_ingredients":[{"type":"heading","ingredient":"blank","heading_text":"Beignets"},{"ingredient":"

1 (7 gram) envelope or 2 ¼ teaspoons rapid rise yeast

","selected_product":null},{"ingredient":"

¼ cup white granulated sugar

"},{"ingredient":"

4 cups bread flour + extra for working the dough

"},{"ingredient":"

½ teaspoon baking soda

"},{"ingredient":"

¾ cup 3 Daughter’s Brewing St. Pete Beach Blonde Ale

"},{"ingredient":"

1 ½ cups buttermilk, shaken

"},{"ingredient":"

½ teaspoon ground nutmeg

"},{"ingredient":"

¼ teaspoon salt

"},{"ingredient":"

Soybean oil, for frying

"},{"type":"heading","ingredient":"blank","heading_text":"Garnish"},{"ingredient":"

2 cups confectioners sugar, for dusting

"},{"ingredient":"

Oatmeal Stout Cream, see recipe below

"},{"ingredient":"

Beach Blonde Crafted Caram-Ale, see recipe below

"},{"type":"heading","ingredient":"blank","heading_text":"Oatmeal Stout Cream"},{"ingredient":"

1 cup 3 Daughter’s Brewing Stern Line Oatmeal Stout

"},{"ingredient":"

2 cups cream cheese, chilled

"},{"ingredient":"

½ cup unsalted butter, room temperature

"},{"ingredient":"

6- 7 cups confectioner’s sugar, sifted

"},{"type":"heading","ingredient":"blank","heading_text":"Beach Blonde Crafted Caram-Ale"},{"ingredient":"

1 (12-ounces) 3 Daughter’s Brewing St. Pete Beach Blonde Ale

"},{"ingredient":"

Zest of 1/2 orange, in large strips

"},{"ingredient":"

½ teaspoon ground cardamom

"},{"ingredient":"

2 tablespoons unsalted butter

"},{"ingredient":"

1 ½ cups brown sugar

"},{"ingredient":"

1 cup heavy cream

"},{"ingredient":"

1 teaspoon vanilla extract

"},{"ingredient":"

Pinch of kosher salt

"}],"recipe_directions":[{"type":"heading","direction":"blank","heading_text":"Beignets"},{"direction":"

In the bowl of a standing mixer fitted with the paddle attachment slowly stir together the yeast, sugar, bread flour, and baking soda.

"},{"direction":"

In a medium sized microwave safe bowl combine the beer and butter. Heat on until the mixture reaches between 120-130°F on a candy thermometer (mixture may look curdled, this is normal), about 2 minutes.

"},{"direction":"

Add the liquid to the dry ingredients, mix on medium speed until all the flour has been incorporated.

"},{"direction":"

Add the nutmeg and salt, turn the mixer on high and beat until the dough forms a soft sticky ball that gathers around the paddle, about 8 minutes.

"},{"direction":"

The dough will be very soft and loose and will hold together when pinched.  If the dough is too loose to hold together add a few pinches of flour.

"},{"direction":"

Transfer to a large, lightly oiled bowl. Loosely cover with a towel or plastic wrap. Allow to rise at room temperature until doubled in size, about 1 hour.

"},{"direction":"

Turn dough out on your work surface that has been dusted with flour.  Press dough into a large rectangle about ½-inch thick. Avoid using a rolling pin in order to preserve the air bubbles in the dough.

"},{"direction":"

Add 3-4 inches of oil to a 4-quart stockpot over medium-high heat. Heat oil to at least 350°, but no hotter than 375°F, adjust heat to stay in that temperate range.

"},{"direction":"

Using a pizza cutter, cut the dough into 2-inch squares. Working in batches, add a few beignets at a time to the oil.  Fry in small batches so that they do not over-crowd each other until they are puffy and golden brown on both sides. Flip them once or twice while frying to make sure they are evenly golden, about 2 minutes.

"},{"direction":"

Remove and drain on a Cookie Sheet with 4 layers of paper towels. Dust with confectioner’s sugar just before serving and serve with a ramekin of Stern Line Oatmeal Stout Cream and Beach Blonde Crafted Caram-Ale.

"},{"type":"heading","direction":"blank","heading_text":"Oatmeal Stout Cream"},{"direction":"

In a small pot cook 1 cup of the Stern Line Oatmeal Stout down until it is reduced to about 3 tablespoons, transfer to a small bowl, skim off any residue, and set to the side.

"},{"direction":"

In the bowl of a standing mixer fitted with the paddle attachment beat butter and cream cheese until light and fluffy on medium speed, about 1 minute. Turn mixer to low and gradually add 6 cups confectioner’s sugar, one cup at a time. Scrape sides and bottom of bowl often. When powdered sugar has been mixed in, the frosting will appear dry.

"},{"direction":"

Gradually add reduced stout and increase mixer speed to medium and beat until light and fluffy, about 2 minutes. Add an additional cup of confectioner’s sugar and beat additional minute it frosting appears too loose.

"},{"direction":"

Scrape frosting into a pastry bag fitted with a star tip. Top beignets with or fill ramekins to serve alongside.

"},{"type":"heading","direction":"blank","heading_text":"Beach Blonde Crafted Caram-Ale"},{"direction":"

Bring the ale, orange zest, and ground cardamom to a gentle boil in a 2 quart Saucier Pan over medium heat; cook, stirring, until reduced to 1 cup, about 10 minutes. Add the butter and brown sugar and cook, stirring only if the mixture looks like it might boil over, until thick and syrupy, about 10 minutes.

"},{"direction":"

Slowly stir in the cream and cook until the sauce thickens, about 5 minutes. Remove from the heat, remove zest with tongs, and stir in the vanilla and salt.

"},{"direction":"

Let the caramel cool slightly, top beignets with or transfer to ramekins and serve alongside beignets as a delicious dip.

"},{"direction":"

Extra sauce will keep refrigerated for up to 2 weeks.

"}],"serving_size":"24 Beignets","prep_time":"20 minutes","cook_time":"15 minutes","recipe_image":"https://f000.backblazeb2.com/file/recipekit-bucket/v1602721133_DSC00348-_1_huvely.jpg","recipe_image_alt_text":null,"iso_prep_time":"PT20M","iso_cook_time":"PT15M","iso_total_time":"PT35M","recipe_rating":"2.7500000000000000","enable_rating":true,"rating_count":"4","recipe_note":null,"recipe_video":null,"recipe_date":"2020-10-14T14:18:17.457+00:00","recipe_calories":null,"recipe_tags":[{"name":"Batter"},{"name":"Beach Blonde Beer"},{"name":"Beach Blonde Beer Beignets"},{"name":"Caram-Ale"},{"name":"Beer"},{"name":"Beer Batter"},{"name":"Beignets"},{"name":"Carmel Sauce"},{"name":"Caramel"},{"name":"Desserts & Breads"},{"name":"Donuts"},{"name":"Sauce"},{"name":"Sweet Treats"}],"nutrition_data":[],"recipe_id":"87981","nutrition_serving_size":null,"nutrition_template":null,"custom_fields":{}}

{"recipe_title":"Sausage, Peppers & Onion Empanadas with Pale Ale Beer Sauce","recipe_author":"

Chef Emily Ellyn

","recipe_description":"

Sausage, Peppers & Onion Empanadas with Pale Ale Beer Sauce is a crowd-pleasing recipe! The small, golden-brown pockets of pastry are stuffed with a savory sausage and pepper mixture and served with a rich, savory beer cheese sauce. A delicious dinner for the family or a tasty way to spice up your party platters!

Cookware Items Used For This Recipe:

  • 4 Quart Stock Pot
  • 2 Quart Saucier
  • Large Cookie Sheet

","recipe_category":"Entreés","recipe_cuisine":null,"recipe_ingredients":[{"ingredient":"

5 tablespoons Unsalted Butter

","selected_product":null},{"ingredient":"

2 pounds Chicken Italian Sausage, casing removed

"},{"ingredient":"

2 sweet Vidalia Onions, small diced

"},{"ingredient":"

⅛ teaspoon of Salt½ teaspoon Freshly Ground Black Pepper

"},{"ingredient":"

⅛ teaspoon of Salt

"},{"ingredient":"

1 Red Bell Pepper, small diced

"},{"ingredient":"

1 Yellow Bell Pepper, small diced

"},{"ingredient":"

1 Poblano Pepper, small diced

"},{"ingredient":"

4 Cloves of Garlic, minced

"},{"ingredient":"

2 tablespoons Fresh Oregano, minced

"},{"ingredient":"

1 tablespoon Fresh Thyme, minced

"},{"ingredient":"

1 (12-ounce) 3 Daughter’s Brewing Beach Blonde Ale

"},{"ingredient":"

1 (12 - 16-ounce) package Smoked Chicken Sausage, chopped fine

"},{"ingredient":"

2 boxes (14.1-ounce) refrigerated Pie Crust

"},{"ingredient":"

1 large Egg whisked together with 1 tablespoon water

"},{"type":"heading","ingredient":"blank","heading_text":"Ingredients Beer Cheese Sauce:"},{"ingredient":"

1 (8-ounce) package Cream Cheese, room temperature

"},{"ingredient":"

1 (8-ounce) block Cheddar Cheese, shredded

"},{"ingredient":"

1 (8-ounce) package of Fresh Mozzarella, rough chop

"},{"ingredient":"

½ teaspoon Smoked Paprika

"},{"ingredient":"

Sea Salt and Black Pepper, to taste

"}],"recipe_directions":[{"direction":"

Place 1 tablespoon unsalted butter, chicken Italian sausage, and Vidalia onions over medium heat in your 4 Quart Stock Pot.

"},{"direction":"

Cook until sausage is brown on all sides and broken into crumbles and the onion is soft and translucent, about 10 minutes.

"},{"direction":"

Add and stir in the bell and poblano peppers, garlic, salt, pepper, oregano, and minced thyme.

"},{"direction":"

Stir in the 3 Daughter’s Brewing Beach Blonde Ale and simmer for 5 minutes or until the peppers are tender.

"},{"direction":"

Place half of the pepper mixture into a 2 Quart Saucierand add 4 tablespoons of butter, cream cheese, cheddar cheese, fresh mozzarella cheese, and smoked paprika.

"},{"direction":"

Whisk together and turn to low allowing mixture to simmer until melted together. Set this Beer Sauce aside.

"},{"direction":"

In your 4-quart Stock Pot, stir in the other half of the sausage mixture and turn to low. Allow it to simmer until the ale is evaporated and the sausage and pepper mixture is coated with a syrupy sauce, about 10-15 minutes.

"},{"direction":"

Meanwhile, preheat oven to 375°F, line twolarge Stainless Steel Cookie Sheet with parchment paper and prepare the empanada dough.

"},{"direction":"

Roll out pie crusts on a clean, floured work surface. Using a cookie cutter or bowl about 6-inches in diameter, press circles into pie crust. Gather the leftover dough, roll it out, and continue cutting circles until all dough is used. Makes about 18 - 20 (6-inch) empanada discs.

"},{"direction":"

"},{"direction":"

"},{"direction":"

"},{"id":1757954989290.5876,"image":"","direction":"

articles.title: Slow Cooker Orange Chicken

image.altText: Bowl of orange chicken served over rice, topped with sesame seeds, green onions, and orange slices

articles.body: There is just something so convenient about making a meal in a slow cooker, especially on a busy schedule! There is so much less clean up and dinner is always ready by the time you get home from work! This super easy and delicious orange chicken recipe pairs so good with rice and is sure to be a family favorite! You can even add in cut up peppers and onions to make sure you get those veggies in! I hope you enjoy this as much as our family does!

{"recipe_title":"Shaved Brussel Sprout Salad with Apples, Goat Cheese & Candied Pecans","recipe_author":"

Amanda Warren

","recipe_description":"

The weather is warming up and with it those big, heavy, filling cold weather dishes may be slowly transitioning into !ighter and healthier colorful plates. This delicious salad is one of my favorites to enjoy anytime of year but especially in the Spring and Summer. I love to pair it with salmon or have it as a nice side dish for those Summer cookouts that are sure to come! This recipe will provide you with everything you need to make the dressing from scratch and to add in the candied pecans that are so addicting on any meal!


Cookware Items Used For This Recipe:

  • Jelly Roll Pan
  • 1 Quart Saucepan
  • 3 Piece Mixing Bowl Set
","recipe_category":"

Lunch, Side Dish or Entreés

10 -12 Cups Shaved Brussel Sprouts

"},{"ingredient":"

1/2 Cup Fresh Strawberries

"},{"ingredient":"

1/4 Balsamic Vinegar

"},{"ingredient":"

1/4 Raw Honey

"},{"ingredient":"

1/2 Cup Olive Oil

"},{"ingredient":"

1/4 Tsp Salt

"},{"ingredient":"

1/4 Tsp Pepper

"},{"ingredient":"

1 Large Apple ( I like the pink lady)

"},{"ingredient":"

4 oz Crumbled Goat Cheese

"},{"ingredient":"

2 Cups Pecans

"},{"ingredient":"

1/4 Cup Maple Syrup

"},{"ingredient":"

2 Tbsp Brown Sugar

"}],"recipe_directions":[{"type":"heading","direction":"blank","heading_text":"Candied Pecans"},{"direction":"

Line Jelly Roll Pan with parchment paper and set aside.

"},{"direction":"

In your 1 Quart Sauce pan, melt together maple syrup and brown sugar until mixed and bubbling.

"},{"direction":"

Add in pecans and coat. Pour onto prepared jelly roll pan and separate nuts so they don’t stick together. Let cool.

"},{"type":"heading","direction":"blank","heading_text":"Delicious Strawberry Balsamic Salad Dressing"},{"direction":"Add strawberries, balsamic vinegar, raw honey, cup olive oil, tsp salt, tsp pepper into blender and blend until smooth."},{"direction":"Place in bowl or dressing dish and set aside for later."},{"type":"heading","direction":"blank","heading_text":"Shave Brussel Sprouts Salad"},{"image":"","direction":"

Shave brussel sprouts. (You can always buy pre shaved however they are always a little thicker and I prefer the shavings small to taste more like a salad and less like brussel’s) To shave them I use my Mandoline slicer on 1/8th. If I am not wanting to slice it, I just buy extra bags of pre sliced and pull out all the thick chunks and use for a side of brussels later in the week.

"},{"direction":"

Assemble the salad in your 3.5 quart stainless steel mixing bowl. I like to put in half of the apples, half the goat cheese and half of the candied pecans add dressing and toss. Once I plate the salad I add a little of each item on the top so you can see the full color and toppings!

","recipe_description":"

There is nothing I love more on a Sunday morning then hot cinnamon rolls with some fresh brewed coffee! I am always trying to create new recipes with varieties of flavors to make it unique! For this recipe I used my tried and true cinnamon roll recipe but added a small twist of blackberry ( which is delicious even by itself) filling and a marscapone frosting that is OUT OF THIS WORLD!

  • 4 Quart Mixing Bowl

","recipe_category":"

"},{"direction":"Once you see yeast grow add in sugar, butter (softened for 15-20 sec in microwave) egg, salt."},{"direction":"Slowly add in flour, once you have added in all 6 cups make sure the dough is slightly sticky and looking like dough. Once you see this, mix for another few minutes. It will start to pull away from the bowl, and If you don’t see this add in more flour until you do."},{"direction":"Sift flour over a clean counter top. Make sure to flour the area outside of where dough is. You will be rolling it out here and you don’t want it to stick later."},{"direction":"Once you have tipped the bowl over and poured out the dough lightly flour the top and cover with a clean kitchen towel."},{"direction":"Let rise for 3 hours."},{"direction":"Once you are about ready to roll dough, melt butter in bowl. Add butter and rest of filling ingredients to blender and milk until it looks like a smoothie."},{"direction":"

When dough is ready, roll out to about 1/4 inch thick in a rectangular form.

"},{"direction":"Pour over the filling mix and evenly spread over the dough."},{"direction":"Next roll dough up for cinnamon rolls! My dough recipe is a little softer than some you may have tried in the past, so if you feel its so soft don’t worry, its going to be delicious!"},{"direction":"

Cut about 2 inch apart and place in your 9x13 bake and roast pan. They will grow in size so pay attention to spacing.

"},{"direction":"Wrap top with saran wrap and put in fridge overnight. Next morning take out and let sit at room temp for 1 hour."},{"direction":"

Bake at 350. Put cinnamon rolls in as the oven is heating to help the pan and rolls adjust to the heat from the fridge (1 hour room temperature they will still be cool to touch)

"},{"direction":"

Bake for 45 min. Check at 25 mins if tops are a golden brown put a layer of foil for rest of cooking time!

"},{"direction":"Once cooked to your liking pour frosting on rolls and enjoy!"},{"type":"heading","direction":"blank","heading_text":"Frosting"},{"direction":"Mix mascarpone and butter until smooth. (if not at room temp warm for 30 seconds in microwave before)"},{"direction":"Add powdered sugar, milk, and vanilla until smooth."}],"serving_size":"8-10","prep_time":null,"cook_time":null,"recipe_image":"https://f000.backblazeb2.com/file/recipekit-bucket/20220526193627-rolls.jpg","recipe_image_alt_text":"Blackberry Cinnamon Rolls","iso_prep_time":null,"iso_cook_time":null,"recipe_rating":"4.0000000000000000","enable_rating":true,"rating_count":"8","recipe_note":"

A couple of tips when using this recipe:

1. You can make them overnight or same day. You will bake less same day because they won’t be cold. Check on them around 25 mins and every 5 mins after.

2. These may be softer then other cinnamon rolls you make when curing and rolling dough. Don’t be worried, this is normal!

3. Don’t worry if you eat more than one.. they are addicting 😉

Amanda Warren

","recipe_description":"

In the middle of a hot Summer and the hottest days of all call for the most delicious treats to make it through! I’m a huge fan of bruschetta, so making this twist on it as a fruity version just seemed so delicious and fit for Summer. You can totally change this up in the fruit department to whatever fruit sounds yummy to you along with whatever is best in season! I did strawberries, cherries and raspberries this time, and it was oh so delicious!Now.. how do you BBQ these little slices of baguette’s? I just found out the way to not burn my 360 cookware griddle on the grill is to put a coat of dish soap on the bottom and MY GOODNESS its genius! The Pan Cleaned so easy! Cannot wait to work on even more recipes for the grill with my favorite 360 pans!

  • 3 Piece Mixing Bowl Set

{"recipe_title":"Birthday Cutout Sugar Cookies","recipe_author":"

Amanda Warren

","recipe_description":"

These may be called “birthday sugar cookies” but I approve them to be eaten on any day all year long! Enjoy them for any celebration, special milestones, or also just because you want a tasty dessert. I love making these for fun and adding a small amount of white chocolate to add décor and to add a little extra sweetness. The cookie itself without the chocolate isn’t overly sweet, so this makes for the ultimate pairing! Hope you enjoy!


Items Used For This Recipe:

  • Large Cookie Sheet
  • 3 Piece Mixing Bowl Set
  • Cookie Cutters

","recipe_category":"

Dessert

","recipe_cuisine":null,"recipe_ingredients":[{"ingredient":"

1 Cup of Melted Butter

"},{"ingredient":"

2 Cups of White Sugar

"},{"ingredient":"

2 Eggs

"},{"ingredient":"

2 tsp Vanilla Extract

"},{"ingredient":"

4 Cups of Flour

"},{"ingredient":"

1/2 tsp Salt

"},{"ingredient":"

1 tsp Baking Soda

"},{"ingredient":"

1 tsp Baking Powder

"},{"ingredient":"

3/4 Cup Buttermilk

"},{"ingredient":"

1/2 Cup Sprinkles

"},{"ingredient":"

White Chocolate for Decorating

"}],"recipe_directions":[{"direction":"

In your Large Mixing Bowl add melted butter and sugar. Beat butter and sugar together until well combined.

"},{"direction":"

Add eggs and vanilla extract, and mix well.

"},{"image":"","direction":"

In another mixing bowl, sift flour, salt, baking soda and baking powder together, and add little by little to butter mixture, alternating with buttermilk.

"},{"image":"","direction":"

Add in sprinkles and mix together until your sprinkles are well combined throughout your cookie dough.

"},{"direction":"

Now that your dough is made, wrap it up in plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 6 hours. I like to let mine sit in the refrigerator overnight for 24 hours. This allows the cutouts to come out perfectly around the edges.

"},{"direction":"

After dough has chilled preheat oven to 375 degrees.

"},{"direction":"

"},{"direction":"

Bake for 8-10 min on 360’s Large Stainless Steel Cookie Sheet.

"},{"image":"","direction":"

After baking place onto cooling rack and decorate once cooled. ENJOY!!

Amanda Warren

","recipe_description":"

I first started making this after getting it in a Home Chef box and thinking it was delicious. Then I thought…this was something different than we normally eat, but so yummy that I decided to make it with my own little twist! I took their recipe and tweaked it just a little by adding a little more garlic, and radishes, along with a few other different ingredients I normally have on hand! It came out super tasty and now is always a favorite in our home. I hope you enjoy it just as much as we do!!


Cookware & Bakeware Items Used For This Recipe:

  • 3 Piece Mixing Bowl Set
  • 3.5 Quart Sauté Pan with cover
  • 2 Quart Saucepan with cover

2 lbs Ground Pork

"},{"ingredient":"

"},{"ingredient":"

1/4 Cup Coconut Aminos

"},{"ingredient":"

1 tbsp Cornstarch

"},{"ingredient":"

1/3 Cup Vegetable Stock

"},{"ingredient":"

1 tbsp Rice Vinegar

"},{"ingredient":"

2 tbsp Brown Sugar

"},{"ingredient":"

"},{"type":"heading","ingredient":"blank","heading_text":"Pickled Veggies:"},{"ingredient":"

"},{"ingredient":"

"},{"direction":"

Start cooking the pork in your 3.5 Quart Sauté Pan over medium heat.

"},{"direction":"

Heat 1 cup of water in your 2 Quart Saucepan until boiling. Add 1 cup of jasmine rice into your boiling water and stir. Once it comes to a boil reduce heat to low and cover with lid. Cook until the water is evaporated. Around 15 minutes.

"},{"direction":"

While pork is cooking on medium heat, you can start making the sauce that goes over top of the pork. Once the pork is fully cooked, pour the pork over your sauce mixture and stir. Let the pork sit in the sauce for 2 minutes and then give it one final good stir and set aside.

"},{"direction":"

{"recipe_title":"Baked Burrata Pumpkin Ziti with Pork Sausage","recipe_author":"

Amanda Warren

","recipe_description":"

Items Used For This Recipe:

  • 3 Quart Saucepan with cover
  • 3.5 Quart Sauté Pan with cover

","recipe_category":null,"recipe_cuisine":null,"recipe_ingredients":[{"ingredient":"

1 lb Ziti

"},{"ingredient":"

4 Tablespoons Butter

"},{"ingredient":"

1 Shallot

"},{"ingredient":"

2 Tablespoons Flour

"},{"ingredient":"

1 Teaspoon Red Pepper Flakes

"},{"ingredient":"

1 Teaspoon Basil

"},{"ingredient":"

1 Teaspoon Oregano

"},{"ingredient":"

1 Cup 100% Pure Pumpkin

"},{"ingredient":"

1 Cup Heavy Cream

"},{"ingredient":"

1 lb Pork Sausage

"},{"ingredient":"

2 Cloves of Garlic

"},{"ingredient":"

1/2 Cup Vegetable Broth

"},{"ingredient":"

1 1/2 Cup Parmesan

"},{"ingredient":"8 oz. Burrata"}],"recipe_directions":[{"direction":"

Prep: Preheat oven to 375 degree temperature. Fill 3 Quart Saucepan with water and bring up to a boil. Mince shallot and garlic cloves. Shred Parmesan. Prep time 5 minutes.

"},{"direction":"

Add butter, garlic and shallots to your 3.5 Quart Sauté Pan and let cook until fragrant and shallots become caramelized.

"},{"direction":"

Add in pork sausage to your sauté pan and cook until it’s done. (you can double the amount of meat in this if you want a more hearty meal as well)

"},{"direction":"

Once sausage is cooked in pan add seasoning; red pepper flakes, basil and oregano. Blend together and add flour. Once the flour is mixed in well add in 100% Pumpkin pure and vegetable broth stirring to marry together.

"},{"direction":"

While cooking sausage and sauce, if water has come to a boil add in 1 lb of ziti to cook. Once al dente drain your paste. Usually this takes 9-11 minutes

"},{"direction":"

Remove your sauté pan from burner and add in your pasta. Once added in continue to stir and add in heavy cream and 1 cup of the parmesan cheese. Make sure to mix it all well.

"},{"direction":"

Once ready to go into oven you will sprinkle the remaining 1/2 cup of parmesan on top and break apart the Burrata as well.

"},{"direction":"

Place in oven and bake for 12-17 minutes until top is bubbly.

"},{"direction":"

ENJOY!!

"}],"serving_size":null,"prep_time":null,"cook_time":null,"recipe_image":"https://f000.backblazeb2.com/file/recipekit-bucket/20221110155242-baked-ziti.jpg","recipe_image_alt_text":"Baked Burrata Pumpkin Ziti with Pork Sausage","iso_prep_time":null,"iso_cook_time":null,"recipe_rating":"1.00000000000000000000","enable_rating":true,"rating_count":"2","recipe_note":null,"recipe_video":null,"recipe_date":"2022-11-10T15:52:57.788+00:00","recipe_calories":null,"recipe_tags":[{"name":"Baked Burrata Pumpkin Ziti with Pork Sausage"},{"name":"Recipe"},{"name":"Pork Sausage Recipe"},{"name":"Baked Burrata Pumpkin Ziti "},{"name":"Baked ziti"},{"name":"Entrees "},{"name":"dinner"},{"name":"pasta dish"},{"name":"fall dish"}],"nutrition_data":[],"recipe_id":"1030186","nutrition_serving_size":null,"nutrition_template":"horizontal","custom_fields":{}}
