{"recipe_title":"The Perfect Homemade Sourdough Bread for Beginners","recipe_author":"

Amanda Warren

","recipe_description":"

Items Used In Recipe:

  • 8 Quart Stockpot with Cover
  • 4 Quart Mixing Bowl

","recipe_category":"

Breads

","recipe_cuisine":null,"recipe_ingredients":[{"ingredient":"

1/3 Cup Sourdough Starter

"},{"ingredient":"

1 - 3/4 Cup Filtered Water

"},{"ingredient":"

1 Tsp Sea Salt

"},{"ingredient":"

4 Cups Bread Flour

"}],"recipe_directions":[{"direction":"

Once sourdough starter is ready to go you will add 1/3 cup to bowl with water and whisk until blended. Add in sea salt and bread flour and mix together with your hands. Flour bread mixture will be scruffy, that's okay. If all flour hasn't blended in you will need a bit more water, but don't over water just enough so your flour is all incorporated. Place a clean towel over the top and let sit for one hour.

"},{"direction":"

After one hour stretch and fold. To stretch and fold you will pick up on one side of the dough pull up and fold into center. Continue around the sides until they have all been picked up and folded into middle. It will normally be around 4-5 times. Cover again and let sit for 30 min. Repeat once more.

"},{"direction":"

After all stretch and folds have finished you will scoop out the dough onto a lightly floured countertop. Using a bench scraper fold under to form a large ball of dough. Make sure to have everything floured so that you prevent sticking to your surfaces.

"},{"direction":"

Once ball is formed you will pick up with your bench scraper and flip over into floured proofing basket. Pinching sides of dough on bottom pull together so the part of the dough showing is creased together. Cover with towel and let sit for 7 - 10 hours.

"},{"direction":"

When you are ready to bake flip your proofing basket with sourdough onto a lightly floured piece of parchment paper. Now you can score your dough and let sit for 30 minutes while you preheat the oven and stockpot.

"},{"direction":"

While your bread is sitting grab your best 360 stockpot, I use the 8 Quart Stockpot with Cover, place in oven and turn on to 450 degrees. Once temperature is reached lower your bread into stockpot holding the sides of the parchment paper. Cover and let bake for 20 minutes. After 20 minutes remove cover and bake an additional 25 minutes or until golden brown.

"},{"direction":"

Baking is all done. Now remove bread and set on cooling rack or cutting board for at least 30 minutes for a resting period before cutting. Your sourdough bread will continue to cook while sitting so cutting too early will cut the full bake time down.

"},{"direction":"8. ENJOY!!"}],"serving_size":null,"prep_time":null,"cook_time":null,"recipe_image":"https://f000.backblazeb2.com/file/recipekit-bucket/20230104201122-sourdough-bread.jpg","recipe_image_alt_text":"The Perfect Homemade Sourdough Bread for Beginners ","iso_prep_time":null,"iso_cook_time":null,"recipe_rating":"3.7631578947368421","enable_rating":true,"rating_count":"38","recipe_note":null,"recipe_video":null,"recipe_date":"2023-01-04T20:11:29.629+00:00","recipe_calories":null,"recipe_tags":[{"name":"Sourdough Bread "},{"name":"Bread"},{"name":"Homemade Sourdough Bread "},{"name":"Beginners Recipe for Bread"},{"name":"Side dish"}],"nutrition_data":[],"recipe_id":"1088145","nutrition_serving_size":null,"nutrition_template":"horizontal","custom_fields":{}}

","recipe_description":"

This flavorful and comforting soup will become a staple in your house. Remember, this minestrone soup is easy to make and is sure to please the entire family. Enjoy!

8 Quart Stock Pot or 6 Quart Stock Pot

","recipe_category":"

","recipe_cuisine":null,"recipe_ingredients":[{"ingredient":"

"},{"ingredient":"

1 Large Onion

"},{"ingredient":"

4 Cloves Minced Garlic

"},{"ingredient":"

5 oz Diced Pancetta

"},{"ingredient":"

1 Cup Chopped Carrots

"},{"ingredient":"

1/4 Cup Chopped Celery

"},{"ingredient":"

1 Zucchini Chopped

"},{"ingredient":"

1 Can Diced Tomatoes (lightly drained)

"},{"ingredient":"

6 Cups Vegetable Broth

"},{"ingredient":"

1 Tablespoon Italian Seasoning

"},{"ingredient":"

2 Bay Leaves

"},{"ingredient":"

Black Pepper (to taste)

"},{"ingredient":"

"},{"ingredient":"

"},{"ingredient":"

2 Handfuls of Spinach, roughly chopped

"},{"ingredient":"

1/2 Cup White Wine

"},{"ingredient":"

2 Tablespoons Basil Pesto

"},{"ingredient":"

Parmesan For Topping

"}],"recipe_directions":[{"direction":"

To make this delicious soup, simply gather all of the ingredients and have them ready. Then, chop the onion, celery, carrots, and garlic. Heat the butter in a large pot over medium-high heat in your favorite stockpot. I love my 8 qt 360 Cookware stockpot for making all soups. Then add the vegetables and cook until they are soft, about 5 minutes.

"},{"direction":"

Next, add the canned tomatoes, pancetta, vegetable broth, Italian seasoning and bay leaf and bring to a boil. Then, add the zucchini, beans and pasta and reduce the heat to low and simmer for 25-30 minutes.

"},{"direction":"

To finish it off, you will stir in the spinach, white wine (I prefer to use Decoy Chardonnay and enjoy the rest of the bottle to serve with the soup), basil pesto and season with pepper to taste. Let ingredients come together for an additional 10-20 minutes or until the spinach has changed color to a dark leafy green.

"},{"direction":"

Serve the soup hot, with a sprinkle of freshly grated Parmesan cheese and slices of crusty bread. Enjoy!

{"recipe_title":"Cherry Chip Cake with Chunks of Dark Chocolate","recipe_author":"

Amanda Warren

","recipe_description":"

Items Used For This Recipe:

  • Cake Pans
  • Mixing Bowls

","recipe_category":"

Dessert

","recipe_cuisine":null,"recipe_ingredients":[{"type":"heading","ingredient":"blank","heading_text":"Cake Batter"},{"ingredient":"6 large eggs"},{"ingredient":"6 large egg whites"},{"ingredient":"2 cup heavy cream"},{"ingredient":"4 tablespoons melted butter"},{"ingredient":"1 tablespoon vanilla extract"},{"ingredient":"1 tsp almond extract"},{"ingredient":"1/2 cup maraschino cherry juice "},{"ingredient":"3 cups sugar"},{"ingredient":"4 1/2 cups cake flour (additional for coating cherries)"},{"ingredient":"2 tablespoon baking powder"},{"ingredient":"1 1/2 teaspoon salt"},{"ingredient":"2 cups grated butter"},{"ingredient":"8 oz dark chocolate chunks"},{"ingredient":"1/2 cup chopped cherries (you will need 10-12 with stems for topping)"},{"type":"heading","ingredient":"blank","heading_text":"Frosting"},{"ingredient":"1 cup butter"},{"ingredient":"8 oz cream cheese"},{"ingredient":"8 cups powdered sugar"},{"ingredient":"1/4 cup heavy cream"},{"ingredient":"1/4 cup cherry juice"}],"recipe_directions":[{"direction":"

Prep by oiling 3 round cake pans and preheat oven to 350 degrees.

"},{"direction":"

Whisk gently together eggs, heavy cream, melted butter, and vanilla in mixing bowl.

"},{"direction":"

In a separate mixing bowl combine dry ingredients.

"},{"direction":"

Grate butter on top of dry ingredients. Combined by hand until butter is no larger than pea sizes.

"},{"direction":"

Next up add in wet ingredients and blend together with electric mixer until well combined on medium speed. Then add in dark chocolate chunk and coarsely chopped flour coated cherries. Coating the cherries will make sure they don't sink to the bottom of the cake while baking in the oven. Using electric mixer until blended once more, making sure to keep on low and not over mixing.

"},{"direction":"

Once combined put into 3 cake pans that are oiled and put into oven. 22-27 min or until wooden pick inserted comes out clean. Once cake is done baking let cool in pan for 15 min and transfer to cooling rack for another 15.

"},{"direction":"

Blend together all frosting ingredients until well combined. (butter and cream cheese should be room temp if not heat in microwave for 30 sec at a time) You can add more heavy cream or powdered sugar depending on desired consistency. I sometimes choose to double the recipe for an even thicker layer on the outside.

"},{"direction":"

Ice layers of cake and do a thin later around for a “crumb layer” that will catch all the crumbs and then make a base for the final layer. Place in fridge for 30 min and then do another layer of frosting. I enjoy piping small circles on top with a piping bag and adding cherries to each one. This also helps when cutting so I know how big to make each slice. Cut, Serve and Enjoy!

"}],"serving_size":null,"prep_time":null,"cook_time":null,"recipe_image":"https://f000.backblazeb2.com/file/recipekit-bucket/20230202200340-cake.jpg","recipe_image_alt_text":"Cherry Chip Cake with Chunks of Dark Chocolate","iso_prep_time":null,"iso_cook_time":null,"recipe_rating":"3.0000000000000000","enable_rating":true,"rating_count":"3","recipe_note":null,"recipe_video":null,"recipe_date":"2023-02-02T20:03:48.831+00:00","recipe_calories":null,"recipe_tags":[{"name":"Dessert"},{"name":"Cake"},{"name":"Cherry Chip Cake with Chunks of Dark Chocolate"},{"name":"Cherry Cake"},{"name":"Baking"}],"nutrition_data":[],"recipe_id":"1123235","nutrition_serving_size":null,"nutrition_template":"horizontal","custom_fields":{}}

","recipe_category":null,"recipe_cuisine":null,"recipe_ingredients":[{"ingredient":"

Using your 360 Slow cooker plug the base in and turn to 3 setting. Add the pot to the stovetop on medium-high heat. Let warm and add butter to the pan and let melt.

"},{"image":"","direction":"

"},{"image":"","direction":"

Get ready for the ultimate comfort food with these juicy, flavor-packed Pulled Pork Sliders! Made with a tender pork shoulder, or butt, seared to perfection and slow-cooked in a rich blend of spices, brown sugar, and broth, this recipe delivers melt-in-your-mouth deliciousness in every bite.

"},{"image":"","direction":"

{"recipe_title":"Apple Glazed Chicken Thighs","recipe_author":"

Amanda Warren

","recipe_description":"

Apple Glazed Chicken Thighs

","recipe_category":null,"recipe_cuisine":null,"recipe_ingredients":[{"ingredient":"

6 Servings

","selected_product":null},{"ingredient":"

6 bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs

"},{"ingredient":"

1 tsp sea salt

"},{"ingredient":"

1/2 tsp black pepper

"},{"ingredient":"

1 tsp onion powder

"},{"ingredient":"

1 tsp garlic powder

"},{"ingredient":"

1/4 tsp paprika

"},{"ingredient":"

2 Tbsp salted butter

"},{"ingredient":"

1 cup apple juice (100% juice)

"},{"ingredient":"

1 teaspoon dried thyme

"},{"ingredient":"

2 medium gala apples

"},{"ingredient":"

1 chopped shallot

"},{"ingredient":"

2 tablespoon dark brown sugar

"}],"recipe_directions":[{"direction":"

Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat, I use my 360 cookware stainless steel pan.

"},{"image":"","direction":"

While pan is heating rinse and pat dry chicken thighs. Make sure to remove any excess moisture to get a crisp edge on the chicken.

"},{"image":"","direction":"

Mix together sea salt, black pepper, onion powder, garlic powder and paprika in a small bowl. Sprinkle the seasoning over chicken on both sides until evenly seasoned.

"},{"image":"","direction":"

Add butter to hot pan and let melt. Add chicken, be sure not to touch for 5-7 minutes until it is crispy on the side and easily comes up from the pan. If it is sticking it is not ready to flip. Flip over on the other side and do the same. Once cooked for at least 5-7 minutes on both side remove and add to a plate, loosely cover and set aside.

"},{"image":"","direction":"

Add an additional 2 tablespoons of butter to same pan and work up any browned bits that formed on pan. Add in chopped shallots and let cook until lightened in color.

"},{"image":"","direction":"

Add in brown sugar and apples. Cooking until apples have softened. Pour in apple juice and let simmer. Stirring for around 5-10 minutes until the liquid begins to thicken. Add chicken back in and coat with a large spoon.

"},{"image":"","direction":"

Bring bold, smoky flavor to your table with this tender and juicy Slow Cooker Brisket recipe, made effortlessly in your 360 stainless steel slow cooker. articles.title: Father’s Day Gifts from 360 Cookware

image.altText: father and sons

articles.body:
Father’s Day is a chance for you to show appreciation to those special men in your life. Whether it’s your own dad, or your partner with whom you’ve established your own family, this June occasion is an opportunity to give them a gift from 360 Cookware they’ll actually use and love.

Of course, all dads are different in their culinary styles. The stereotypical man is the king of the barbeque, and of course 360 Cookware has the perfect pieces to upgrade his patio cooking game. On the other hand, if dad is a keen chef or baker, we have a complete line of cookware and bakeware to delight him on his special day! Let’s look at some particular gifts that might tickle his fancy.

Grilling Set

The backyard barbeque can become much more versatile with the addition of some quality stainless steel pieces from 360 Cookware. Our 360 Grilling Set consists of our Mini Jelly Roll Pan and Jelly Roll Pan. Designed to withstand high heat without warping, they’re made of three layers: an outer and inner layer of non-toxic surgical grade stainless steel, with a middle layer of aluminum to ensure even heat distribution across the entire pan.

These handy pans can be used directly on the grill for roasting vegetables for a tasty side dish to accompany grilled meats, or for cooking a roast on a grill or in a smoker, keeping the juices from dripping down into the flames. Of course, they’re not limited to use on the barbeque!

Griddle

If dad wants to fry up a batch of bacon on the barbeque to top some burgers, he’ll definitely appreciate the 11-Inch Square Griddle, and it’s equally at home on the stovetop inside. Big enough to handle four grilled cheese sandwiches at once, it is made of the same high-quality stainless steel and aluminum layers as the Grilling Set. Customers love the long, ergonomic handle which delivers both comfort and safety when cooking over high heat.

Breakfast Set

The griddle is also one of the stars of our 360 Breakfast Set, along with a saucepan with lid, fry pan, and jelly roll pan. {"recipe_title":"Pumpkin Tiramisu Recipe","recipe_author":"

Amanda Warren

","recipe_description":"","recipe_category":null,"recipe_cuisine":null,"recipe_ingredients":[{"ingredient":"

6 large egg yolks, room temperature

","selected_product":null},{"ingredient":"

1 cup granulated sugar

"},{"ingredient":"

1 1/2 cups cold heavy whipping cream

"},{"ingredient":"

16 oz mascarpone cheese

"},{"ingredient":"

1 teaspoon vanilla extract

"},{"ingredient":"

2 teaspoons pumpkin pie spice

"},{"ingredient":"

1/2 cup pumpkin puree

"},{"ingredient":"

3/4 cup espresso, cooled

"},{"ingredient":"

2 tablespoons granulated sugar

"},{"ingredient":"

1/2 teaspoon pumpkin pie spice

"},{"ingredient":"

4 packs of ladyfingers

"},{"ingredient":"

2 tablespoons cocoa powder

"},{"ingredient":"

1/4 teaspoon pumpkin spice seasoning

"}],"recipe_directions":[{"id":1755884951552.6653,"direction":"

In a heat safe bowl, whisk together egg yolks & sugar until well combined. Place the bowl over: a sauce pan with simmering water. Make sure the bowl does not touch the water or you have too much water. Whisk continuously until the mixture thickens and feels hot to touch. Should be around 10 minutes. Make sure a film on top does not form, if you continue to whisk the entire time you will be fine. Remove from heat and let cool to room temp.

"},{"id":1755885228013,"image":"","direction":"

﻿﻿﻿In a new bowl whip heavy cream with a hand mixer until stiff peaks form. Place in fridge to chill until later.

"},{"id":1755885251231,"image":"","direction":"

In a third bowl mix together mascarpone until smooth. Whisk in cooled egg mixture until well combined together. Do not over mix where it becomes runny. Add in pumpkin pie spice and puree. Lastly fold in whipped cream until fully incorporated

"},{"id":1755885262465,"image":"","direction":"

Assemble the Tiramisu! In a wide bowl add espresso, sugar and pumpkin pie spice. Stir until sugar has dissolved.

"},{"id":1755885275314,"image":"","direction":"

﻿﻿﻿Start dipping the lady fingers into mixture quickly. Dip on each side no more then one second on each side but making sure they are fully saturated. Place in your dish for the tiramisu, Use your 360 bake & roast pan. You'll make a single layer until pan is filled completely.

"},{"id":1755885285684,"image":"","direction":"

﻿﻿﻿Add half of the egg/heavy cream mixture over the lady finger layer and evenly layer cross. Repeat the process above. Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for 4 hours or overnight (the longer it stays in the fridge the better it tastes) before serving.

"},{"id":1755885296884,"image":"","direction":"

Finish off by dusting the top with a mixture of cocoa powder & pumpkin spice seasoning. Serve & Enjoy!

"}],"serving_size":null,"prep_time":null,"cook_time":null,"recipe_image":"https://f000.backblazeb2.com/file/recipekit-bucket/20250910181632-processed-7ab9477a-d925-42bf-915c-958e31a0a3a4-20-1.jpeg","recipe_image_alt_text":"Pumpkin Tiramisu Recipe","iso_prep_time":null,"iso_cook_time":null,"recipe_rating":"3.7500000000000000","enable_rating":true,"rating_count":"4","recipe_note":null,"recipe_video":null,"recipe_date":"2025-08-22T17:55:02.098+00:00","recipe_calories":null,"recipe_tags":[],"nutrition_data":[],"recipe_id":"2340583","nutrition_serving_size":null,"nutrition_template":"horizontal","custom_fields":[{"name":"","value":""},{"name":"","value":""}]}

Amanda Warren

","recipe_description":"","recipe_category":null,"recipe_cuisine":null,"recipe_ingredients":[{"ingredient":"6 baby pumpkins"},{"ingredient":"1/4 teaspoon sea salt"},{"ingredient":"1/4 teaspoon black pepper"},{"ingredient":"4 tablespoons salted butter"},{"ingredient":"1 small Fresno pepper, finely chopped"},{"ingredient":"1 onion, diced"},{"ingredient":"2 cups chicken chopped into bite size pieces"},{"ingredient":"6 oz gruyere cheese"},{"ingredient":"6 oz walnuts, chopped"},{"ingredient":"1 tablespoon chives"},{"ingredient":"1/2 cup salted butter"},{"ingredient":"1 cup heavy cream"},{"ingredient":"1 cup white wine"},{"ingredient":"Juice of half a lemon"},{"ingredient":"1/4 teaspoon sea salt"},{"ingredient":"1/4 teaspoon black pepper"}],"recipe_directions":[{"id":1759521030349.6448,"image":"","direction":"

Preheat oven to 400 degrees. Line a baking pan or baking sheet with parchment paper and set aside.

"},{"id":1759521030349.7388,"image":"","direction":"

Clean your pumpkins with soap and water, dry and cut the tops off in a circle shape. Wide enough to eat out of later. Scrape the sides and clean out all the pumpkin seeds and stringy pulp. Brush insides and outsides of pumpkin (and the top) with 2 tablespoons of melted butter. Sprinkle with sea salt and pepper. Place on parchment lined baking pan and bake in oven for 45 -60 minutes or until softened.

"},{"id":1759521030349.554,"image":"","direction":"

Meanwhile while pumpkins bake mix together the filling. In a large pan melt the remaining 2 tablespoons of butter, sauté onion and small Fresno pepper (can omit if not wanting any spice). Once onions become transparent in color add into bite-size pieces of chicken and cook (or you can also use precooked chicken). Once cooked add to a large bowl and mix with cheese and walnuts.

"},{"id":1759521030349.1736,"image":"","direction":"

When pumpkins are done in oven stuff with chicken mixture and return to oven for another 20 minutes.

"},{"id":1759521030349.057,"image":"","direction":"

While pumpkins cook make the creamy sauce to go over top. In a small saucepan heat butter until melted. Add in wine, heavy cream and lemon juice and simmer on low until starts to thicken. Make sure you are stirring occasionally. Add in salt and pepper (more or less to taste). Set aside when done and when pumpkins are completely finished drizzle over the inside to your liking. Sprinkle with chives. Then, serve, enjoy and happy harvest!

"}],"serving_size":null,"prep_time":null,"cook_time":null,"recipe_image":"https://f000.backblazeb2.com/file/recipekit-bucket/20251003201638-processed-3581dc09-9f60-49bf-bda9-7c147a1da8d3.jpeg","recipe_image_alt_text":"Walnut Chicken Stuffed Pumpkins","iso_prep_time":null,"iso_cook_time":null,"recipe_rating":"1.00000000000000000000","enable_rating":true,"rating_count":"1","recipe_note":null,"recipe_video":null,"recipe_date":"2025-10-03T19:51:31.703+00:00","recipe_calories":null,"recipe_tags":[],"nutrition_data":[],"recipe_id":"2392008","nutrition_serving_size":null,"nutrition_template":"horizontal","custom_fields":[{"name":"","value":""},{"name":"","value":""}]}

{"recipe_title":"Strawberry Puff Pastry","recipe_author":"

Amanda Warren

","recipe_description":"
Delicious Puff Pastries!
","recipe_category":"","recipe_cuisine":"","recipe_ingredients":[{"id":"0-split-0-1771021936464","type":"ingredient","index":1,"isNew":true,"ingredient":"2 cups (335 grams) sliced strawberries , fresh or frozen","selected_product":null},{"id":"0-split-1-1771021936464","type":"ingredient","index":2,"isNew":true,"ingredient":"1 tablespoon lemon juice","selected_product":null},{"id":"0-split-2-1771021936464","type":"ingredient","index":3,"isNew":true,"ingredient":"1 tablespoon lemon zest","selected_product":null},{"id":"0-split-3-1771021936464","type":"ingredient","index":4,"isNew":true,"ingredient":"⅔ cup (130 grams) granulated sugar","selected_product":null},{"id":"0-split-4-1771021936464","type":"ingredient","index":5,"isNew":true,"ingredient":"½ teaspoon vanilla extract","selected_product":null},{"id":"0-split-5-1771021936464","type":"ingredient","index":6,"isNew":true,"ingredient":"2 puff pastry","selected_product":null},{"id":"0-split-6-1771021936464","type":"ingredient","index":7,"isNew":true,"ingredient":"1 large egg , lightly beaten (for egg wash, optional)","selected_product":null},{"id":"0-split-7-1771021936464","type":"ingredient","index":8,"isNew":true,"ingredient":"1 cup (113 grams) powdered sugar","selected_product":null},{"id":"0-split-8-1771021936464","type":"ingredient","index":9,"isNew":true,"ingredient":"1-2 tablespoons heavy cream or mil","selected_product":null}],"recipe_directions":[{"id":"0-split-7-1771021943190-split-0-1774368322591","type":"direction","image":null,"index":9,"direction":"

Start by making the filling. Add strawberries, lemon juice and zest, and sugar in a medium sauce pan and set over medium high heat. Stir and mash with a large fork and bring to a boil. Boil for about 2-3 minutes until sugar is dissolved and combined.

"},{"id":"0-split-7-1771021943190-split-1-1774368322591","type":"direction","image":null,"index":10,"direction":"

Reduce heat to medium low. Continue to simmer for 10-15 minutes until thickened. Add vanilla extract. Cool to room temperature before spooning onto the prepared pastry squares. Any leftovers may be stored in the fridge for a few weeks.

"},{"id":"0-split-7-1771021943190-split-2-1774368322591","type":"direction","image":null,"index":11,"direction":"

Make pastry squares but unfolding puff pastry and cutting into long rectangles (around 3 per puff pastry). Fill one side with strawberry filling, making sure to leave edging around to close the puff pastry.

"},{"id":"0-split-7-1771021943190-split-3-1774368322591","type":"direction","image":null,"index":12,"direction":"

Once finished filling, make an egg wash with egg & water. Brush along the edges of the puff pastry. Unfold 2 puff pastry sheet on a lightly floured surface. Cut into 12 equal sized squares. Prick each square a few times with a fork.

"},{"id":"0-split-7-1771021943190-split-4-1774368322591","type":"direction","image":null,"index":13,"direction":"

Add 1-2 tablespoons of the strawberry puree you made into the middle of 6 squares. Spread out, but not right to the edge. Leave a little bit of a border.

"},{"id":"0-split-7-1771021943190-split-5-1774368322591","type":"direction","image":null,"index":14,"direction":"

Use a brush to add the egg mixture onto the sides. Add a puff pastry square on top of the square with strawberry filling. With a fork, pinch the edges to seal the two squares together. Repeat until you have 6 puff pastries. Brush the top with remaining egg mixture and lay on your cookie sheet. Bake for 20-23 minutes or until golden brown.

"},{"id":"0-split-7-1771021943190-split-6-1774368322591","type":"direction","image":null,"index":15,"direction":"

While the puff patries are baking, make your icing. Add powdered sugar, strawberry puree, and milk to a small bowl. Mix well until you have a consistency that drizzles. Add a little more sugar or milk if needed.

"},{"id":"0-split-7-1771021943190-split-7-1774368322591","type":"direction","image":null,"index":16,"direction":"

Once your puff pastries are done, transfer them to a wire rack and let them cool. Then drizzle with icing and sprinkles if desired.

"}],"serving_size":"","prep_time":null,"cook_time":null,"recipe_image":"https://f000.backblazeb2.com/file/recipekit-bucket/20260217163051-20260209-114041372.jpg","recipe_image_alt_text":"Strawberry Puff Pastry Recipe","iso_prep_time":null,"iso_cook_time":null,"recipe_rating":"3.0000000000000000","enable_rating":true,"rating_count":"5","recipe_note":"","recipe_video":"","recipe_date":"2026-02-13T22:33:00.042+00:00","recipe_calories":null,"recipe_tags":[],"nutrition_data":[],"recipe_id":"2584453","nutrition_serving_size":"","nutrition_template":"horizontal","custom_fields":[]}

articles.title: Can You Use Stainless Steel For Sourdough?

image.altText: sourdough bread on a rack

articles.body:
Sourdough: Everything Old is New Again

Archeologists have found evidence of leavened bread made from wild yeasts from as far back as 3700 BCE, so sourdough has a very long history. The commercial yeast we’re used to picking up in the grocery store has only been around for a couple of centuries, and before then, bread was made with sourdough or discarded yeast from brewing beer. 

When people found themselves stuck in their homes during the early days of the pandemic, one of the ways they kept themselves busy was by rediscovering the joys of baking with sourdough. This truly ancient baking technique has regained a place in many homes, and with good reason! Not only is sourdough good for you, but it’s delicious, and once you’ve mastered the basics, remarkably easy to prepare, especially when using quality stainless steel from 360 Cookware!

Why Stainless Steel is Ideal for Baking Sourdough

If you look at any sourdough site online (and there are MANY), you’ll probably find somewhere the advice not to use metal utensils, bowls, or cooking surfaces with sourdough. It is true that aluminum and copper can react with the acids in the sourdough and leach toxins into your sourdough. Nonstick pans are also a bad choice for baking sourdough. Some brands start releasing toxic fumes at temperatures as low as 365°F, while a loaf of bread is best baked at temperatures well above that!

On the other hand, stainless steel is non-reactive and has no coatings to leach toxins into your food, making it an ideal choice for baking your loaf of sourdough bread. While cast iron is often recommended, a high-quality pan such as a 360 Cookware stockpot is an excellent choice for baking an artisan boule. Its 3-ply construction, with a layer of high-conductive aluminum sandwiched between two layers of surgical-grade stainless steel, ensures excellent heat distribution to bake your loaf evenly. When you move on to sandwich loaves, buns, and other sourdough breads, you’ll find that our loaf pans, jelly roll pans, and baking pans will be perfect for all your sourdough baking needs!

Getting Started with Sourdough

To make a loaf of sourdough bread, you need to start with a sourdough starter. Don’t worry about fancy equipment: this process is simple and cheap. You’ll need a glass quart jar (reusing an old one is fine), and preferably an inexpensive kitchen scale for measuring accurately.

You can make your own starter by mixing 60 g of flour and 60 g of water in equal quantities in a glass jar. It’s best to use water that hasn’t been chlorinated or softened. Start with white all-purpose or bread flour, as that will give you more versatility than using whole wheat or rye flour. If you have organic grapes on hand, you can add a few whole ones to the mixture, as the natural yeasts on the fruit can help to jump-start the process.

Tie a piece of cheesecloth over the top of the jar. The mixture needs to breathe, and wild yeast has to be able to get to your flour and water mixture, but fruit flies especially will be drawn irresistibly to the yeasty mixture unless you keep them out. Set the jar in a warm corner and leave it to develop for a couple of days.

Every day after that, remove half of the mixture from the jar, and discard it (NOT down the sink, as it will clog your pipes!). Add another 60 g each of water and flour, and stir until smooth, and return to its warm spot. By the end of 7 days or so, you should have a bubbling, spongy mixture, ready to use to make a loaf of bread!

If this process sounds intimidating, you may know someone who has a starter that they’d be happy to share with you, and you can also buy sourdough starter from baking supply sites online.

Many sourdough bakers recommend keeping your starter on the counter all the time, and going through the discarding/feeding process every day to keep it fresh and active. You’ll end up accumulating a lot of discard, which can be used to make a variety of baked goods, including crackers and quick breads.

However, if you prefer to skip the discard, you can instead keep a small amount of your sourdough starter stored in the refrigerator until you’re planning to bake. Bring it out, and add flour and water equal to the total amount required for your recipe. For instance, if you’re baking a loaf of bread that needs 100 grams of starter, add 50 g of flour and 50 g of water. Mix it well, and put it in a warm spot for several hours until it’s doubled in size and bubbly. Then, after you’ve measured out your starter for the recipe, just put the lid back on and pop the jar back in the refrigerator until you need it again! 

Mixing and Proofing Sourdough

For your first adventure in sourdough baking, start with the simplest of recipes, a basic artisan loaf. The recipe couldn’t be easier:

  • 150 g active starter
  • 250 g water
  • 25 g olive oil
  • 10 g salt
  • 500 g all-purpose or bread flour

In a large bowl, stir together everything but the flour until mixed well. Then add the flour and stir until it forms a shaggy, rough dough. Cover it with a damp tea towel and let it sit for half an hour. Then, for a total of 4 times, every half hour, uncover the dough and start by pulling up an edge and folding it over towards the center. Then, go around the dough and repeat 3 or 4 times. Cover the bowl again and let it rest for another half hour before repeating.

Once you’ve done this 4 times, your rough, shaggy dough will have been transformed into a smooth, elastic ball as the gluten develops and the sourdough yeasts start to work. Now, cover the bowl (if you have a silicone lid, that’s a perfect choice, but plastic wrap will work too) and let it complete its bulk fermentation at room temperature for 8 to 10 hours. It should almost double in volume and have a few surface bubbles. When you poke the dough, it should spring back slowly but not completely. Then it’s ready. 

While you can proceed to shape the dough for final proofing at this point, you can also put the covered bowl in the refrigerator overnight. 

Shaping and Final Proofing

If you look online, you’re going to see many bakers using bannetons to shape their sourdough loaves for final proofing. Don’t feel that you need to invest all that money in fancy equipment right away, though. A ceramic or stainless steel bowl and a sheet of parchment paper will work just fine!

Once your sourdough has passed the poke test, dump it out of the proofing bowl onto a lightly floured surface. Form it into a loose ball and let it rest for 30 minutes before proceeding to the shaping. 

After the dough has rested, lightly flour the top and then turn it over so the sticky side faces you. Stretch it out gently into a rough rectangle, and then start by folding the lower third up to the center, pinching the dough so that the fold is sealed. Then, do the same with the top of the dough, making sure it overlaps the seam. Next, take the lower right-hand and upper left-hand corners and pull them together in the middle, and then do the same with the opposite corners. Flip it over so the seam side is down. 

At this point, the dough should be in the shape of a smooth ball. Tighten up the surface by dragging it gently across the counter until it’s taut and smooth. Place it in the bowl lined with a sheet of parchment paper, and cover it. At this point, you can let it rise on the counter for a couple of hours, or put it in the refrigerator to rise slowly for 8-12 hours before continuing with baking. 

If you prefer to use a stainless steel loaf pan, grease it or line it with parchment paper. After folding the dough from the top and bottom, sealing the seams, pull the top corners into the center and seal them down. Finally, complete the first two folds again, securing the seals each time. Place it seam-side down in the prepared loaf pan, cover with a cloth, and let it rise until it’s reached the top of the pan sides.

Baking Sourdough in Stainless Steel

About half an hour before baking, place your covered pan into the oven, and set the temperature at 450°F. You want both the oven and pan to be good and hot before adding the dough. Slash across the top of your loaf with a sharp knife or razor blade, and carefully lift it onto the parchment paper and place it in the pan. Throw in a couple of ice cubes, replace the lid, and return the pan to the oven. After 30 minutes, remove the lid, and leave it for 15 more minutes. When the crust is golden brown, and an instant-read thermometer registers around 205°F in the center of the loaf, remove the loaf from the pan and let it cool completely on a rack before cutting into it.

If you’re using a loaf pan, let the oven heat to 375°F. Set a shallow pan with a handful of ice cubes on the lower rack, and place the loaf pan on the middle rack and let the bread bake for 35-45 minutes when an instant-read thermometer registers around 205°F in the center of the loaf.

Congratulations! You’ve baked your first loaf of sourdough bread! Now you can explore the many websites and books dedicated to the world of sourdough. Enjoy!

articles.title: Can Stainless Steel Go in the Oven? What to Know Before You Bake
articles.body:
If you’re asking, can I put a stainless steel pan in the oven, the answer is Yes! Fully clad stainless steel pans are usually designed to move seamlessly from the stovetop to the oven, and are oven-safe to around 500-600°F. The only variables to consider are the composition of knobs and lids when determining if you can put a stainless steel pan in the oven, so it’s a good idea to do your research before buying stainless steel cookware or bakeware.

Summary Box: High-quality stainless steel cookware is designed to be used in ovens, making it a versatile and practical choice.

Why Stainless Steel Withstands Oven Heat

Even the hottest oven is no match for stainless steel, which melts at over 2,500°F. Obviously your kitchen oven will get nowhere even close to that temperature, as residential ovens usually top out at 550°F.

Quality fully clad stainless steel has no coating to degrade at high temperatures and withstands warping much better than single-ply pans.

What Actually Limits Oven Safety

COMPONENT

TYPICAL RISK

WHAT TO CHECK

Handles

and Lid Knobs

·   Plastic handles will melt in the oven

·   Silicone-wrapped handles are safe to 400-500°F, depending on the brand

·   Phenolic handles vary in heat resistance

·   Riveted stainless steel handles are safe to 500°F

Check the individual manufacturer’s specifications to ensure that the handles are safe in the oven.

Glass Lids

Tempered glass lids can shatter above 350°F, while stainless steel lids are resistant to about 500°F

Check if the cookware comes with glass or stainless steel lids, and the specific brand’s recommendations for maximum safe temperature

Aluminum/Copper Cores or Disc Bottoms

·   Fully clad pans with a middle layer of aluminum or copper will resist warping and are usually safe to 550-600°F

·   Disc bottom pans may have an exterior aluminum pad attached to the bottom which could come loose when exposed to high heat

Look at the construction of the cookware before purchasing; fully clad pans will last longer and distribute heat more evenly

Coatings

Nonstick coatings, even on a stainless steel pan, are not safe at temperatures above 480°F.

Pay attention to manufacturer’s warnings about maximum safe temperatures

 

Stainless Steel Oven-Safe Temperatures by Type

So, can stainless steel pans go in the oven? Yes, but there’s no one stainless steel oven-safe temperature, even for fully clad pans. It all depends on the individual brand, so make sure that you check the manufacturer’s guidance.

  • Pans that are all stainless steel with no other materials are usually oven-safe to anywhere between 500-800°F, depending on the brand.
  • Pans with silicone-wrapped handles can resist heat up to between 400-500°F.
  • Tempered glass lids are usually safe only to 350°F, although some brands have a recommendation as high as 400°F.

Are 360 Cookware Stainless Steel Pans Oven-Safe?

Yes, 360 Cookware stainless steel pans are safe to 500°F. This includes the Vapor© Technology lids, as well as the handles. They’re all made from high-quality stainless steel, with a layer of aluminum sandwiched between layers of surgical-grade stainless steel. There is nothing to melt or warp. This means that our pieces can go straight from the stovetop to the oven for a seamless cooking experience.

Stovetop to Oven: When It's Worth It

There are many techniques that involve starting a dish on the stovetop and then moving it to the oven to finish cooking. Let’s look at a few favorites and see how 360 Cookware pans make it easy!

Pan-Seared Steak

The best way to ensure a steak with a perfect outer crust and a juicy, flavorful interior is to pan-sear it and then finish it in a hot oven. And a 360 Cookware 11.5” fry pan gives you lots of room to cook up a delicious steak dinner for two!

A rib eye, New York strip, or sirloin are all great choices for this dish. Whichever cut you choose, pull the steaks out of the refrigerator about an hour before cooking. Salt both sides and let them rest and reach room temperature.

Set the oven to 400°F. Pat the steaks dry and rub them with a drizzle of olive or avocado oil, and any seasoning you’d like to add. Preheat the fry pan over a medium burner until droplets of water dance across the surface rather than evaporate, and lightly coat the pan with oil.

Place the steaks into the pan, and don’t try to move them until the surface has seared and naturally released from the pan. Flip them over and repeat on the other side. Now that you have a nice crust, move the pan into your pre-heated oven.

After 2 minutes for a 1-inch thick steak, or 8 minutes for a 2-inch steak, pull the pan out and test with an instant-read thermometer. At this point your goal is a temperature 5 degrees less than your desired final temperature. For instance, if you want your steak rare, or at 130°F, it’s finished in the oven at 125°F. You then will cover it with a loose tent of aluminum foil for 5 to 10 minutes to rest and let the juices reabsorb before serving. Do not use the pan lid for this step, as it will trap in steam and the steak’s crust will soften.

Frittata

While you could use a fry pan to cook a frittata, the higher sides on our 3.5 Quart Sauté Pan will more easily accommodate our veggie frittata recipe. It’s a simple process: preheat the oven to 375°F, preheat the pan over medium heat, and sauté your vegetables in a splash of olive oil. Pour the eggs beaten with milk over it all, add cheese, and once the edges have started to set, transfer the pan to the oven to finish cooking. It’s then ready to move straight to the table for serving.

Braising

In essence, braising is the slow cooking of meat or vegetables in liquid without boiling. This is especially useful with tougher cuts of meat, as the low and slow heat breaks down the collagen surrounding the muscle fibers, with the end result being tender and luscious. Think pot roast or pulled pork!

You could simply put a piece of meat into an oven-safe pot, add broth and seasonings, and pop it into a slow oven to cook for hours. However, you get superior flavor by searing the meat first, and that’s where using an oven-safe pot like our 6-quart stock pot comes in.

Preheat your oven to 300°F and set your stock pot on a medium burner until the water drops dance across the heated surface. Drizzle your preferred cooking oil, and then briefly sear all sides of your meat. Remove them before proceeding.

Add your chopped aromatics such as onions, celery, and carrots, and any seasonings called for in your recipe. Once they’ve softened, pour in your braising liquid, preferably a rich broth, with possibly some wine to add more depth of flavor. Then return the meat to the pot, cover, and place in the oven for 2 to 3 hours.

Because our stock pot comes with Vapor© Technology, you don’t even have to check it periodically to add more liquid. The tight seal will ensure that your broth will infuse the meat without evaporating.

Roasting Chicken Thighs

Our Stainless Steel Roasting Pan will take care of all stages of cooking our recipe for Lemon Rosemary Chicken & Root Vegetables, and still look good enough to take straight to the table for serving!

Tips For Using Stainless Steel in the Oven

Bear in mind the following tips for using stainless steel cookware in the oven:

  • Preheat gradually and don't move a pan from a cold fridge straight into a hot oven.

  • Handles get hot, so always use mitts. Some cooks drape a towel over the handle as a reminder.

  • Because of the higher temperatures involved, broiling should only be done with stainless steel pans with no other materials

  • Deglazing is an easy technique that will give you the most delicious pan sauce after oven roasting, as well as making clean-up easier.

When Not to Put Stainless Steel in the Oven

Not all stainless steel pans are safe for oven use. Anything with plastic or wooden handles should only be used on the stovetop, as plastic could melt and wood could become charred and damaged.

Be very cautious about using glass lids. Even the best ones are only good to 350°F, and if you don’t know what the rating is on your lids, they may not even be safe at that temperature.

Finally, even a good quality stainless steel pan should not be left empty for long under a broiler.

How To Clean Stainless Steel After Oven Use

Check out how to clean even burnt-on food from stainless steel. Because stainless steel pans don’t have a nonstick coating to worry about, you can get more vigorous in getting off even the most stubborn grease.

You may see a rainbow discoloration even after you’ve thoroughly cleaned your stainless steel pan, but not to worry! It’s completely harmless and easy to get rid of. When stainless steel is exposed to high temperatures, such as in a hot oven, the chromium in the steel may react with oxygen to form chromium oxide on the surface. It’s purely cosmetic, but if it bothers you, all you need is vinegar. Pour some into the pan, let it sit for a minute, and then rinse and wipe. No more rainbow!

FAQ

Can stainless steel go under the broiler?

Stainless steel is safe under the high heat of a broiler. And with 360 Cookware’s 3-ply construction, you won’t have to worry about the pan warping, as the aluminum core will distribute heat evenly across the entire body. However, make sure there’s at least 2 inches clearance between the pan and the flame, and don’t add the pan until the broiler has preheated, which should take about 5 minutes.

Can a stainless steel pot go in the oven?

360 Cookware stainless steel pots that do not have glass lids or plastic or wood handles are safe in the oven to 500°F. This makes it easy to start a dish on the stovetop and then move it to the oven to finish cooking.

Can stainless steel lids go in the oven?

Stainless steel lids are oven-safe if they do not have plastic or wood knobs. However, many stainless steel lids, even with fully clad pans, are single-layer and could warp under high heat. On the other hand, 360 Cookware’s Vapor© technology lids are especially suited to use in the oven, as they are 3-ply with an aluminum core, just like the body of the pan, ensuring even heat distribution from all directions and resistance to warping.

What temperature is stainless steel safe to?

Stainless steel is usually safe to 500°F, although it’s best to check the individual manufacturer’s specifications to ascertain what they recommend.

Will the oven discolor my stainless pan?

When stainless steel is exposed to very high heat, it may develop a rainbow discoloration, but it’s harmless and easy to remove with a quick soak in vinegar.

Can I put a cold stainless pan in a hot oven?

It is not recommended to move a stainless pan directly from the refrigerator to a hot oven. For instance, if you’ve prepared a dish in our Casserole Pan for serving the next day, let it sit out on the counter for 15 minutes before placing it in the pre-heated oven, or set it into a cold oven and then turn on the heat.

How to Measure a Pan

If you’re going to be using a baking pan that is not the same dimensions that your recipe calls for, it’s important to find out first if the batter is going to fit, or if you’ll have to adjust the quantities to ensure success.

The first and most important thing to know is that you always measure the inside of the pan, not the outside! Many pans, including 360 Cookware’s, are thick enough that measuring the outside of the pan will give you an inaccurate calculation of the pan’s capacity.

In most cases, measure the width of the pan across the top edge rather than the base. Always measure from the inner edges, rather than the outer lip.

It’s also important to include the height of the pan in your calculations. Simply stand your ruler up inside the pan, away from the sides if they’re sloped.

You can easily determine the capacity of the pan by simply adding water a cupful at a time. When it’s full, you’ll know exactly how much your pan can hold! Remember, though, that most baked goods such as cakes or quick breads will rise as they bake, so your goal is to only have enough batter to fill the pan to 2/3 full at most.

Which Size Do You Need?

Most home cooks will find themselves reaching for the same baking pans time after time, but they won’t necessarily be the same for every household. A lot depends on the size of your family and what things you usually bake. Buying a few key pieces and making the occasional recipe adjustments will ensure that you have the pans you need without cluttering up your bakeware shelves with rarely-used items.

Round vs Square Pans

The classic 9x9” square pan is a natural choice for many bakers, but a 9” round pan has advantages over the square one. Let’s take the example of cinnamon rolls, a favorite choice for Sunday brunch. Baked in a square pan, the rolls in the four corners are going to get the most direct heat on two sides, and as a result will be finished sooner than the rolls in the center, or even the rolls that are tucked between the corner pieces along the sides.

However, in a round pan, all the rolls along the outside curved edge will have the same amount of surface exposure, and so they will bake more evenly, leaving a couple of gooier ones tucked in the center for those who prefer that texture. The only downside is that because a 9” round pan is a bit smaller in volume, you might need to settle for seven or eight rolls rather than the nine that fit in a 9x9” square pan.

Round pans work equally well for cakes and fruit crisps, so if you want to get just one small baking pan, you will find the round version to be a more versatile choice.

Rectangular Casserole Pan

If you have a larger family, or are hosting guests, or even doing some meal prepping for the week, a larger pan is invaluable. The classic 9x13” rectangular bake and roast pan is a must to cook up a large batch of lasagna or bake a sheet cake for a potluck dessert.

Loaf Pan

Whether you’re baking a quick banana bread, a classic pound cake, or a loaf of crusty bread, you’re going to find the standard 10x5” loaf pan to be an invaluable addition to your kitchen. Even if you’re just a household of two, try halving a cheesecake recipe and baking it in the loaf pan so that both of you get to enjoy a couple of delicious slices without days of leftovers sitting in the fridge.

Substituting Sizes

At least starting out, you’re unlikely to have every configuration of baking pan in your kitchen, but that doesn’t mean you can’t easily adapt any recipe to what you’ve got available. Let’s break it down for you:

This may seem overwhelming when faced with a complex recipe using lots of ingredients, but there are apps out there like Inch Calculator’s Recipe Scale Conversion Calculator to take care of all the number crunching for you! And this is one time that using metric measurements with a digital scale will really come in handy, as it’s easier to measure in grams rather than fiddly fractions of teaspoons and cups.

But what to do about the eggs, you ask? Well, if you’re dividing a recipe for a smaller pan, crack the egg into a bowl, beat it up, measure the total and use whatever fraction you need for the recipe. The rest can be thrown into scrambled eggs the next day. Or if you’re multiplying a recipe and end up needing an egg and a half, add an extra 2 tablespoons of liquid egg whites with one whole egg to make up the difference. It is important to try to keep the total egg volume correct, especially with cakes and cookies.

Will you need to adjust the baking time when you’re scaling a recipe up or down? Probably not if you’ve calculated correctly, as the batter depth should remain consistent. However, if you’ve changed pans without adjusting the recipe size, the baking time will change based on the depth of the batter. Deeper means a longer bake time, while shallower will need less time in the oven.

If you have a deeper batter, you want to make sure that the outside edges don’t get overbaked before the center is done, so lower the baking temperature by 25˚F, and start checking for doneness once you’ve exceeded the original baking time by 10% or so. So, if a cake was supposed to bake at 350˚F for 40 minutes, set the oven at 325˚F and start checking the center at around 45 minutes.

For a shallower batter in a larger pan than the recipe calls for, switch things around. Keep the temperature the same but start checking early, because it will be done ahead of time. Better to be safe than sorry!

 

360 Cookware Sizes

Round Cake Pan

Whether you opt for the basic pan with no handles, or the deluxe version with handles, every kitchen needs this classic 9x2” cake pan. It’s perfect for baking a cake, a batch of cinnamon rolls, or fruit crisp.

Rectangular Bake & Roast Pan

This classic 9x13x2” bake pan, with or without handles, is an invaluable piece when you’re making a big batch of cinnamon rolls for Christmas brunch or a sheet cake for a birthday party.

Brownie Pan

We call it this 9x2” round pan a brownie pan, but it’s definitely not a one-trick pony! While it will bake up a batch of perfectly chewy brownies or a giant cookie, it’s also an excellent choice for heating up a quick dish for two in the toaster oven, or even for baking thin layers for a multi-layer cake.

Loaf Pan

With interior dimensions of 10x5x25/8”, you’re going to love this pan for baking the perfect loaf of crusty bread or a tender banana bread.

FAQ

How much batter goes in a 9x9” pan?

A 9x9” square pan has a total volume of 10 cups, but you won’t be using that much batter, because you have to leave room for the cake to rise without spilling over the sides of the pan. Most recipes for a 9x9” pan will yield about 5 cups of batter to allow for this.

Can I use an 8” pan instead of a 9"?

If you are baking a cake and want to change from a 9x9” square pan to an 8x8” square pan, you will have to multiply your recipe by .79 to scale it down to fit into the smaller pan. Otherwise, your batter will end up spilling over the sides as it rises. If you are baking bar cookies or a fruit crisp, you don’t have to worry about that, but the additional depth of the ingredients will change the length of time that it takes to be done. Lower the baking temperature by 25˚F and increase the time by about 20%, or use the same calculation of .79 to scale down the recipe.

What size is a standard brownie pan?

Brownies can be baked in different sizes of pans, but the 8” square pan is often used for family-sized batches. They can also be baked in 9” square pans or 10x13” pans. As long as the depth of the batter remains constant, done by scaling the recipe up or down to fit the pan, they will bake at the same temperature and length of time.
